source.title: p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties
source.venue: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 1 (2013), e1, 77 pp.; corrigendum Forum of Mathematics, Pi 4 (2016), e6
readSections: The whole published article, §§1–9 and the references, pp. 1–77 (Cambridge Core open-access PDF, fetched 29 September 2026), with every quoted formula checked on page images; and the complete 4-page corrigendum (doi:10.1017/fmp.2016.4), whose corrections are applied to the items. The published text was compared word by word with arXiv:1205.3463v2 (3 Nov 2012): the differences are copyediting and an expanded introductory overview, with no change of statements found. Cambridge stamps each download, so the file hash is not reproducible; the recorded hash is of the pdftotext -layout text with the download-stamp lines removed. The review found one numbering difference: the published version adds Lemma 5.8 (completely continuous maps of Banach spaces), which makes explicit a step of arXiv v2's proof of Lemma 5.6 ('one easily checks that A is a subquotient of a bounded subset of a finite-dimensional K-vector space'), so published Lemmas 5.9, 5.11, Definition 5.10 and Corollary 5.12 are arXiv v2's 5.8, 5.10, 5.9 and 5.11. Blueprint packets cite arXiv numbering.

summary: Scholze builds the pro-étale site X_proét of a locally noetherian adic space over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) (§3, with the 2016 corrigendum's corrected covers). On it he defines the completed structure sheaves Ô_X⁺, Ô_X and their tilts, shows that affinoid perfectoid objects form a basis on which Ô_X⁺ is almost acyclic (§4), and deduces that connected affinoids are K(π,1) for p-torsion coefficients. From these and a theory of almost finitely generated 𝒪-modules (§2), he proves the primitive comparison theorem: H^i(X_ét, 𝕃) ⊗ 𝒪_K^a/p ≅ H^i(X_ét, 𝕃 ⊗ 𝒪_X^{+a}/p) for X proper smooth over an algebraically closed complete K and 𝕃 an F_p-local system. It gives finiteness of étale cohomology of proper smooth rigid-analytic varieties, with a relative version (§5). He constructs the period sheaves A_inf, B_inf, B⁺_dR, B_dR and the structural de Rham sheaves 𝒪B⁺_dR, 𝒪B_dR (the latter corrected by the corrigendum), and proves the Poincaré lemma and the structure of 𝒪B_dR on small affinoids (§6). He builds a fully faithful functor from filtered modules with integrable connection to B⁺_dR-local systems, and defines de Rham lisse ℤ_p-sheaves (§7). He proves the de Rham comparison theorem with coefficients for proper smooth rigid spaces over a discretely valued field. It gives degeneration of the Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence, the Hodge–Tate decomposition (Theorem 8.4, answering Tate's question) and a relative version (Theorem 8.8) (§8). §9 collects relative GAGA over affinoids (Köpf) and finiteness facts. The atlas was built on this paper. PadicHodgeTheory P8 and P8:local-rational, AdicEtaleGeometry A1 and PerfectoidSpaces P0–P6 already cite it and its corrigendum. The comparison statements of §8 are planned in P8 and CohomologyComparisons CP.3, the pro-étale covers and site axioms in AdicEtaleGeometry A1 and DiamondsAndVStacks D0, and the period sheaves and Poincaré lemma in P8:local-rational. Of 254 items, 58 are planned, 5 are in Mathlib (the ring-level period rings A_inf with θ, B⁺_dR, B_dR, and Bézout ideals) and 191 are missing. The missing ones are the steps between the layers' headline targets: the K(π,1) and primitive-comparison and finiteness theorems, the §2 almost-module theory, the details of X_proét and its structure sheaves, the §7 functor and §9's GAGA. All 191 go as sources of existing layers: PadicHodgeTheory P8 (93 items), PerfectoidSpaces P0/P2/P6 (60), AdicEtaleGeometry A1 (32) and AdicSpacesPartII R1/R3 (6). No new roadmap or Part II is needed.

items.name: Theorem 1.1: finiteness of F_p-étale cohomology of proper smooth rigid spaces
items.statement: Let K be a complete algebraically closed extension of ℚ_p, let X/K be a proper smooth rigid-analytic variety, and let 𝕃 be an 𝔽_p-local system on X_ét. Then H^i(X_ét, 𝕃) is a finite-dimensional 𝔽_p-vector space for all i ⩾ 0, which vanishes for i > 2 dim X.
items.note: Proved in §5 as Theorem 5.1 (p. 38), stated there for proper smooth adic spaces over Spa(K, K⁺). The proof uses the §2 classification (Proposition 2.6 in Lemma 5.4, Lemma 2.12 in Lemma 5.11), Kiehl-style finiteness and an Artin–Schreier argument. Searched research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/*.json and research/blueprint/roadmaps/*.json for 'finite-dimensional', 'finiteness', 'primitive comparison', 'rigid-analytic'. No stage plans it. ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H3–H5 plan finiteness only for curves or constructible complexes in Huber's setting, and PadicHodgeTheory P8 / CohomologyComparisons CP.3 consume a comparison but do not state this theorem. This agrees with PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-18/085 (status missing). The paper remarks that properness is essential and smoothness is probably unnecessary.

items.name: Theorem 1.2: connected affinoids are K(π,1) for p-torsion coefficients
items.statement: Let X be a connected affinoid rigid-analytic variety over K. Then X is a K(π, 1) for p-torsion coefficients: that is, for all p-torsion local systems 𝕃 on X, the natural map H^i_cont(π₁(X, x), 𝕃_x) → H^i(X_ét, 𝕃) is an isomorphism. Here, x ∈ X(K) is a base point, and π₁(X, x) denotes the profinite étale fundamental group.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Proved in §4 as Theorem 4.9 (p. 35). That version is stated for an affinoid connected noetherian adic space X = Spa(A, A⁺) over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p), with a geometric point x̄. No smallness or smoothness hypothesis. Searched research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/*.json and research/blueprint/roadmaps/*.json for 'K(π', 'K(\pi', 'fundamental group' combined with 'p-torsion'. Used in §8 (Proposition 8.2) to compare lisse sheaves on X_ét and X_proét.

items.name: Almost vanishing of H^i(U_ét, O⁺/p) on affinoid perfectoids
items.statement: On affinoid perfectoid subsets U (of X_proét), H^i(U_ét, 𝒪_X⁺/p) is almost zero for i > 0, where 𝒪_X⁺ ⊂ 𝒪_X is the subsheaf of functions of absolute value ⩽1 everywhere.
items.note: Recalled in the introduction as 'the basic finiteness result', related to Faltings' almost purity. It is proved precisely in §4, Lemma 4.10 (p. 36), from [17] (Perfectoid spaces). PerfectoidSpaces:P3 plans it: 'Glue the affine tilting equivalence to the equivalence of étale sites, ECD 6.3, and prove the étale almost-acyclicity assertion.'

items.name: Almost finite generation of H^i(X_ét, O⁺/p)
items.statement: For X proper (and smooth) over K, H^i(X_ét, 𝒪_X⁺/p) is almost finitely generated over 𝒪_K; this is deduced from the almost acyclicity of 𝒪_X⁺/p on affinoid perfectoids and a suitable cover of X by affinoid perfectoid subsets in X_proét, by an argument modelled on Kiehl's proof of finiteness of coherent cohomology of proper rigid-analytic varieties [12].
items.note: This is the intermediate step announced for Theorem 1.1. It is carried out in §5, Lemmas 5.3–5.6 (pp. 38–43), with 'almost finitely generated' in the sense of Definition 2.3 and Proposition 2.6. Searched research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/*.json and research/blueprint/roadmaps/*.json for 'almost finitely'. No stage plans it. AdicSpacesPartII R3 plans only coherent 'Kiehl-type proper finiteness/coherence'.

items.name: Theorem 1.3 (absolute): primitive comparison theorem
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 1.1 (K a complete algebraically closed extension of ℚ_p, X/K a proper smooth rigid-analytic variety, 𝕃 an 𝔽_p-local system on X_ét), there is an almost isomorphism of 𝒪_K-modules for all i ⩾ 0, H^i(X_ét, 𝕃) ⊗ 𝒪_K/p → H^i(X_ét, 𝕃 ⊗ 𝒪_X⁺/p).
items.note: Proved in §5 as the second assertion of Theorem 5.1 (p. 38): an isomorphism of almost K⁺-modules H^i(X_ét, 𝕃) ⊗ K^{+a}/p ≅ H^i(X_ét, 𝕃 ⊗ 𝒪_X^{+a}/p). It is closely related to [6, §3, Theorem 8] (Faltings). Searched research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/*.json and research/blueprint/roadmaps/*.json for 'primitive comparison'. IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.3 only uses 'the precise primitive comparison' as an input; no stage proves it. This agrees with the Zavyalov and BMS18 extractions, which leave it missing. Used for Equation (1.1) and for Theorem 8.4.

items.name: Theorem 1.3 (relative): primitive comparison for proper smooth morphisms
items.statement: Assume that f : X → Y is a proper smooth morphism of rigid-analytic varieties over K, and 𝕃 is an 𝔽_p-local system on X_ét. Then there is an almost isomorphism for all i ⩾ 0, (R^i f_ét∗ 𝕃) ⊗ 𝒪_Y⁺/p → R^i f_ét∗(𝕃 ⊗ 𝒪_X⁺/p).
items.note: Proved in §5 as Corollary 5.12 (pp. 47–48), for proper smooth morphisms of locally noetherian adic spaces over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p). The almost setting there is relative to Y_ét, O_Y⁺ and the ideal of elements of valuation < 1 everywhere. The proof checks stalks at geometric points using [9, Proposition 2.6.1] (Huber) and Theorem 5.1. Remark 1.4: under algebraicity and integral-model hypotheses this is [6, Section 6, Theorem 6], and here it is a direct corollary of the absolute case. Searched research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/*.json and research/blueprint/roadmaps/*.json. No stage plans it.

items.name: Lisse ℤ_p-sheaf as a locally free Ẑ_p-module on X_proét
items.statement: Let Ẑ_p = lim← ℤ/pⁿℤ as sheaves on X_proét. A lisse ℤ_p-sheaf 𝕃 on X can be defined as a locally free Ẑ_p-module on X_proét.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/lisse-zp-sheaf (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. The formal definitions are in §8: Definition 8.1 (p. 66) gives lisse ℤ_p-sheaves on X_ét as inverse systems, and lisse Ẑ_p-sheaves on X_proét as sheaves locally isomorphic to Ẑ_p ⊗_{ℤ_p} M with M a finitely generated ℤ_p-module. Proposition 8.2 proves the two notions equivalent, using Theorem 4.9 and Lemma 3.18. So 'locally free' in the introduction is loose: M may have torsion. Searched research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/*.json and research/blueprint/roadmaps/*.json for 'lisse', 'Ẑ_p', 'ℤ_p-local system'. VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories VS3 is about lisse categories on v-stacks, a different notion.

items.name: The B⁺_dR-local system 𝕄 = 𝕃 ⊗_{Ẑ_p} 𝔹⁺_dR
items.statement: Among the period sheaves on X_proét is 𝔹⁺_dR, the relative version of Fontaine's ring B⁺_dR. A lisse ℤ_p-sheaf 𝕃 on X gives rise to a 𝔹⁺_dR-local system 𝕄 = 𝕃 ⊗_{Ẑ_p} 𝔹⁺_dR on X_proét.
items.note: 𝔹⁺_dR is defined in §6 (Definition 6.1, p. 49), and the tensor construction is used in Definition 8.3 and Theorem 8.4. PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational plans the sheaf: 'Construct the rational structural B_dR and crystalline/semistable period sheaves from the same rings as R06.1.' Forming 𝕃 ⊗ 𝔹⁺_dR is then immediate.

items.name: Equation (1.1): B⁺_dR-comparison as formal consequence of Theorem 1.3
items.statement: For a lisse ℤ_p-sheaf 𝕃 on X (proper smooth over K) with 𝕄 = 𝕃 ⊗_{Ẑ_p} 𝔹⁺_dR, it is a formal consequence of Theorem 1.3 that H^i(X_ét, 𝕃) ⊗_{ℤ_p} B⁺_dR ≅ H^i(X_proét, 𝕄).   (1.1)
items.note: Proved in §8, in the proof of Theorem 8.4 (pp. 67–68): Theorem 5.1 gives the A_inf version, then p is inverted, then one passes through B_inf/(ker θ)^k using Lemma 3.18. PadicHodgeTheory:P8 plans 'the proper-smooth comparison with connection and tensor compatibility'. CohomologyComparisons:CP.3 plans 'the comparison after B_dR-inversion with p-adic étale cohomology' for constant coefficients.

items.name: Theorem 1.5: fully faithful functor from filtered O_X-modules with integrable connection to B⁺_dR-local systems
items.statement: Let X be a smooth rigid-analytic variety over k, where k is a complete discretely valued nonarchimedean extension of ℚ_p with perfect residue field. Then there is a fully faithful functor from the category of filtered 𝒪_X-modules with an integrable connection satisfying Griffiths transversality, to the category of 𝔹⁺_dR-local systems.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/associated-bdr-plus-local-system (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Proved in §7: Definition 7.4, Theorem 7.6 (pp. 59–60), which gives ℳ = Fil⁰(ℰ ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒪𝔹_dR)^{∇=0}, and the sentence after it: 'the notion of being associated gives rise to a fully faithful functor'. It uses Brinon's period rings [4] and his Galois-cohomology computations. Searched research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/*.json and research/blueprint/roadmaps/*.json for 'integrable connection', 'Griffiths', 'Riemann–Hilbert'. HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T6:comparison plans only a logarithmic Riemann–Hilbert for canonical local systems, and PadicHodgeTheory P8 plans only period sheaves, the Poincaré lemma and the proper comparison. Uses the corrected 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR of the corrigendum (Def. 6.8).

items.name: De Rham lisse ℤ_p-sheaf
items.statement: A lisse ℤ_p-sheaf 𝕃 is de Rham if the associated 𝔹⁺_dR-local system 𝕄 lies in the essential image of the functor of Theorem 1.5.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/de-rham-lisse-sheaf (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. The formal version is §8, Definition 8.3 (p. 67), for X proper smooth over Spa(k, O_k); §7 Definition 7.5 gives the notion of 'associated'. P8 plans only the comparison with connection. Earlier extractions (CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17/12, BETTS-STIX-25/38) route theorems that use this notion to P8, but not the definition. Marked missing.

items.name: Claim: the Rapoport–Zink conjecture on local systems on period domains fails for non-minuscule μ
items.statement: The form of the correspondence of Theorem 1.5 indicates that the Rapoport–Zink conjecture on the existence of local systems on period domains (see [15]) is wrong if the cocharacter μ is not minuscule: in that case it asks for a crystalline, and thus de Rham, local system on (an open subspace of) the period domain whose associated filtered module with integrable connection does not satisfy Griffiths transversality, whereas the p-adic Hodge theory formalism does not allow for an extension of Theorem 1.5 beyond the situations where Griffiths transversality is satisfied.
items.note: An informal remark, not proved in the paper. It follows from Theorem 7.6: any de Rham local system's filtered module satisfies Griffiths transversality. [15] = Rapoport–Zink, Period spaces for p-divisible groups. Searched research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/*.json and research/blueprint/roadmaps/*.json for 'Rapoport', 'minuscule'. No stage plans it.

items.name: Theorem 1.6 (i): Galois-equivariant B⁺_dR comparison with coefficients
items.statement: Let k be a discretely valued complete nonarchimedean extension of ℚ_p with perfect residue field κ, and algebraic closure k̄, and let X be a proper smooth rigid-analytic variety over k. For any lisse ℤ_p-sheaf 𝕃 on X with associated 𝔹⁺_dR-local system 𝕄, we have a Gal(k̄/k)-equivariant isomorphism H^i(X_k̄, 𝕃) ⊗_{ℤ_p} B⁺_dR ≅ H^i(X_k̄, 𝕄).
items.note: Proved in §8 as the first assertion of Theorem 8.4 (pp. 67–68), from Theorem 5.1 via A_inf, B_inf/(ker θ)^k and Lemma 3.18. PadicHodgeTheory:P8: 'apply CohomologyComparisons CP.3–CP.4 to the proper-smooth comparison with connection and tensor compatibility'.

items.name: Theorem 1.6 (ii): degeneration of the Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence for de Rham coefficients
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 1.6, if 𝕃 is de Rham, with associated filtered module with integrable connection (ℰ, ∇, Fil^•), then the Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence H^{i−j,j}_Hodge(X, ℰ) ⇒ H^i_dR(X, ℰ) degenerates.
items.note: Proved in §8, Theorem 8.4 (p. 68). The proof uses the freeness of H^i(X_k̄, 𝕄), Theorem 7.11 and a dimension count. P8 plans 'the proper-smooth comparison with connection'. CohomologyComparisons:CP.3 plans 'Prove filtration strictness and the Hodge–Tate/de Rham spectral-sequence comparisons in characteristic zero, with proper smoothness', but only for constant coefficients.

items.name: Theorem 1.6 (iii): H^i(X_k̄, 𝕃) is de Rham with D_dR = H^i_dR(X, ℰ)
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 1.6 with 𝕃 de Rham, associated with (ℰ, ∇, Fil^•), H^i(X_k̄, 𝕃) is a de Rham representation of Gal(k̄/k) with associated filtered k-vector space H^i_dR(X, ℰ).
items.note: Proved in §8, Theorem 8.4, which gives a filtration-preserving Gal(k̄/k)-equivariant isomorphism H^i(X_k̄, 𝕃) ⊗_{ℤ_p} B_dR ≅ H^i_dR(X, ℰ) ⊗_k B_dR. That in turn uses Theorem 7.11. P8 plans the proper-smooth comparison with connection.

items.name: Theorem 1.6 (iv): Hodge–Tate decomposition with coefficients
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 1.6 with 𝕃 de Rham, associated with (ℰ, ∇, Fil^•), there is a Gal(k̄/k)-equivariant isomorphism H^i(X_k̄, 𝕃) ⊗_{ℤ_p} \hat{k̄} ≅ ⊕_j H^{i−j,j}_Hodge(X, ℰ) ⊗_k \hat{k̄}(−j).
items.note: Proved in §8, Theorem 8.4 (p. 68), from Theorem 7.11 (the isomorphism H^i(X_k̄, gr⁰𝕄) ≅ ⊕_j H^{i−j,j}_Hodge(X, ℰ) ⊗_k \hat{k̄}(−j)). Here \hat{k̄} is the completion of k̄. P8 plans the proper-smooth comparison with connection.

items.name: Remark 1.7: Hodge cohomology of a filtered module with integrable connection
items.statement: The Hodge cohomology H^{i−j,j}_Hodge(X, ℰ) is defined as the hypercohomology of the associated graded of the de Rham complex of ℰ, with the filtration induced from Fil^•.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/proper-smooth-bdr-local-system-comparison (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Made precise in Theorem 7.11: H^{i−j,j}_Hodge(X, ℰ) = H^i(X, gr^j(DR(ℰ))). Searched research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/*.json and research/blueprint/roadmaps/*.json. DerivedDeRhamCohomology and CP.3 treat only the constant case.

items.name: Corollary 1.8 (i): Hodge–de Rham degeneration for proper smooth rigid spaces
items.statement: For any proper smooth rigid-analytic variety X over k (k a discretely valued complete nonarchimedean extension of ℚ_p with perfect residue field), the Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence H^i(X, Ω^j_X) ⇒ H^{i+j}_dR(X) degenerates.
items.note: Theorem 1.6 / Theorem 8.4 with 𝕃 = Ẑ_p, (ℰ, ∇, Fil^•) = (𝒪_X, d, trivial). The paper gives no separate proof. It answers a question of Tate [18, Remark on p. 180], and needs no Kähler hypothesis. CohomologyComparisons:CP.3: 'Prove filtration strictness and the Hodge–Tate/de Rham spectral-sequence comparisons in characteristic zero, with proper smoothness and convergence.' CP.3 works over C via BMS1 §13, with descent to X_0/K ('When X descends to a proper smooth X_0/K, compare ...').

items.name: Corollary 1.8 (ii): Hodge–Tate decomposition for proper smooth rigid spaces
items.statement: For any proper smooth rigid-analytic variety X over k, there is a Hodge–Tate decomposition H^i(X_{k̄,ét}, ℚ_p) ⊗_{ℚ_p} \hat{k̄} ≅ ⊕_{j=0}^{i} H^{i−j}(X, Ω^j_X) ⊗_k \hat{k̄}(−j).
items.note: Theorem 1.6 with 𝕃 = Ẑ_p, after inverting p. There is no separate proof. CohomologyComparisons:CP.3 plans the 'Hodge–Tate/de Rham spectral-sequence comparisons in characteristic zero, with proper smoothness', in its constant-coefficient B_dR⁺ framework. The paper states the decomposition as Gal(k̄/k)-equivariant only via Theorem 1.6.

items.name: Corollary 1.8 (iii): H^i(X_{k̄,ét}, ℚ_p) is de Rham with D_dR = H^i_dR(X)
items.statement: For any proper smooth rigid-analytic variety X over k, the p-adic étale cohomology H^i(X_{k̄,ét}, ℚ_p) is de Rham, with associated filtered k-vector space H^i_dR(X).
items.note: Theorem 1.6 / 8.4 with 𝕃 = Ẑ_p. CohomologyComparisons:CP.3: 'When X descends to a proper smooth X_0/K, compare that deformation with H_dR(X_0/K) tensor_K B_dR^+', together with the comparison after B_dR-inversion with p-adic étale cohomology.

items.name: Corollary 1.9: twisted Hodge–de Rham degeneration for quotients of Drinfeld's upper half-space (Schneider's conjecture)
items.statement: Let k be a finite extension of ℚ_p, let X = Ω^n_k be Drinfeld's upper half-space, which is the complement of all k-rational hyperplanes in ℙ^{n−1}_k, and let Γ ⊂ PGL_n(k) be a discrete cocompact subgroup acting without fixed points on Ω^n_k. One gets the quotient X_Γ = X/Γ, which is a proper smooth rigid-analytic variety over k. Let M be a representation of Γ on a finite-dimensional k-vector space such that M admits a Γ-invariant 𝒪_k-lattice. It gives rise to a local system ℳ_Γ of k-vector spaces on X_Γ. Then the twisted Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence H^i(X_Γ, Ω^j_{X_Γ} ⊗ ℳ_Γ) ⇒ H^{i+j}_dR(X_Γ, 𝒪_{X_Γ} ⊗ ℳ_Γ) degenerates.
items.note: Conjectured by Schneider [16, p. 633]. Deduced from Theorem 1.6, with no written proof. The lattice gives a lisse ℤ_p-sheaf, which must be shown de Rham with associated module 𝒪_{X_Γ} ⊗ ℳ_Γ (trivial filtration), because ℳ_Γ is trivialized by the Γ-covering Ω^n_k → X_Γ. Searched research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/*.json and research/blueprint/roadmaps/*.json for 'Drinfeld', 'Schneider', 'upper half'. No stage plans it.

items.name: Poincaré lemma for 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR (announced)
items.statement: Over X_proét (X smooth over k) one has an exact sequence of sheaves 0 → 𝔹⁺_dR → 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR →^∇ 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR ⊗_{𝒪_X} Ω¹_X →^∇ ⋯. Here 𝔹⁺_dR is what [1, 4] call 𝔹^{∇+}_dR and 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR is what they call 𝔹⁺_dR.
items.note: Proved in §6 as Corollary 6.13 (p. 54), with ∇ Griffiths-transverse and the sequence strict exact. It follows from Proposition 6.10, and uses the CORRECTED definition of 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR from the 2016 corrigendum: the ker θ-adic completion of (R_i⁺ ⊗̂_{W(κ)} A_inf(R, R⁺))[1/p], with a strengthened Proposition 6.10. PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational: 'Prove rational local acyclicity, filtration strictness and the relative Poincaré lemma'. The P8 description also says: 'Apply Scholze’s 2013 corrigendum throughout P8'.

items.name: Theorem 1.10: higher direct images of de Rham lisse sheaves are de Rham
items.statement: Let k be a discretely valued complete nonarchimedean extension of ℚ_p with perfect residue field κ, and let f : X → Y be a proper smooth morphism of smooth rigid-analytic varieties over k. Let 𝕃 be a lisse ℤ_p-sheaf on X which is de Rham, with associated filtered module with integrable connection (ℰ, ∇, Fil^•). Assume that R^i f_proét∗ 𝕃 is a lisse ℤ_p-sheaf on Y; this holds true, for example, if the situation arises as the analytification of algebraic objects. Then R^i f_proét∗ 𝕃 is de Rham, with associated filtered module with integrable connection given by R^i f_dR∗(ℰ, ∇, Fil^•).
items.note: Proved in §8 as Theorem 8.8 (pp. 71–72), using the relative Poincaré lemma (Proposition 8.5), Lemmas 8.6–8.7 and Remark 8.9, which checks the algebraic case via Theorem 9.3. PadicHodgeTheory:P8: 'apply CohomologyComparisons CP.3–CP.4 to the proper-smooth comparison with connection and tensor compatibility'. This matches the routing of CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17/12 and BETTS-STIX-25/38.

items.name: Setup of §2: K, Γ, v, log Γ, π^r, 𝔪
items.statement: Let K be a nonarchimedean field, i.e. a topological field whose topology is induced by a nonarchimedean norm |·| : K → ℝ_{⩾0}, with value group Γ = |K^×| ⊂ ℝ_{>0} dense. Let 𝒪 ⊂ K be the ring of integers, and fix π ∈ 𝒪 topologically nilpotent (|π| < 1). Using the logarithm with base |π|, identify ℝ_{>0} with ℝ; this induces a valuation v : K → ℝ ∪ {∞} with v(π) = 1, and log Γ ⊂ ℝ denotes the induced subgroup. For each r ∈ log Γ fix an element π^r ∈ K with |π^r| = |π|^r. The maximal ideal 𝔪 of 𝒪 is generated by all π^ε, ε > 0, and satisfies 𝔪² = 𝔪. An 𝒪-module M is almost zero if 𝔪M = 0.
items.note: The almost-mathematics base (𝒪, 𝔪) is planned by PerfectoidSpaces:P0: 'Construct almost-zero modules, the Serre quotient, almostification …'. It is instantiated with 'the ideal generated by the positive fractional powers of a pseudouniformizer' and 'prove idempotence'. The valued-field setup (Mathlib Valued / ValuationRing) exists, but 𝔪² = 𝔪 for a dense rank-one valuation is not stated as a lemma. π must be nonzero for the logarithm to make sense (implicit in the paper, which normalises v(π) = 1).

items.name: Definition 2.1: the category of almost 𝒪-modules
items.statement: The category of 𝒪^a-modules, or almost 𝒪-modules, is the quotient of the category of 𝒪-modules modulo the category of almost zero modules. M ↦ M^a denotes the functor from 𝒪-modules to 𝒪^a-modules.
items.note: PerfectoidSpaces:P0: 'Construct almost-zero modules, the Serre quotient, almostification and its adjoints'. The paper uses it with 𝔪 as in the §2 setup. Tau Ceti has no almost-mathematics files: grep -ri 'almost' in TauCeti/TauCeti finds only unrelated uses, e.g. 'almost everywhere'.

items.name: Definition 2.2: the relations M ≈_ε N and M ≈ N
items.statement: Let M and N be two 𝒪-modules. For any ε > 0, ε ∈ log Γ, we say that M ≈_ε N if there are maps f_ε : M → N, g_ε : N → M such that f_ε g_ε = g_ε f_ε = π^ε. Moreover, if M ≈_ε N for all ε > 0, we write M ≈ N.
items.note: Searched research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/*.json and research/blueprint/roadmaps/*.json and Tau Ceti/Mathlib for 'almost', '≈_ε'. Not in P0, which plans only almost-zero, almost-flat and almost-finite-projective notions. This is the paper's nonstandard approximate-isomorphism relation, used throughout §2 and in §5.

items.name: Properties of ≈_ε and ≈
items.statement: The relations ≈_ε and ≈ are symmetric, and transitive in the sense that M ≈_ε N and N ≈_δ L imply M ≈_{ε+δ} L; in particular ≈ is transitive. M is almost zero if and only if M ≈ 0. For two 𝒪-modules M, N, if M^a ≅ N^a as 𝒪^a-modules then M ≈ N, but the converse is not true.
items.note: Stated without proof. Example 2.4(i) shows the converse fails: I_r ≈ 𝒪 but I_r^a ≇ 𝒪^a for r ∉ log Γ. Depends on Definition 2.2, which no stage plans.

items.name: Definition 2.3: almost finitely generated / almost finitely presented 𝒪-modules
items.statement: Let M be an 𝒪-module. Then M is called almost finitely generated (respectively almost finitely presented) if for all ε > 0, ε ∈ log Γ, there exists some finitely generated (respectively finitely presented) 𝒪-module N_ε such that M ≈_ε N_ε.
items.note: Planned: PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented (PerfectoidSpaces--P0 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PerfectoidSpaces--P0.json, merged before this extraction. Searched research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/*.json and research/blueprint/roadmaps/*.json for 'almost finitely', 'almost-finitely'. There are no hits in any Perfectoid/PadicHodge stage. PerfectoidSpaces:P0 plans 'almost-flat and almost-finite-projective modules' but not almost finite generation or presentation (Gabber–Ramero). No Mathlib or Tau Ceti declaration.

items.name: Almost finite generation/presentation depends only on M^a
items.statement: The property of being almost finitely generated (respectively almost finitely presented) depends only on the 𝒪^a-module M^a, so one may speak of almost finitely generated (respectively presented) 𝒪^a-modules.
items.note: Planned: PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented (PerfectoidSpaces--P0 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PerfectoidSpaces--P0.json, merged before this extraction. Stated without proof. It follows from the remark after Definition 2.2 (M^a ≅ N^a ⇒ M ≈ N) and transitivity of ≈_ε.

items.name: Example 2.4(i): finitely generated ideals of 𝒪 are principal
items.statement: Any finitely generated ideal of 𝒪 is principal.
items.note: Mathlib: 𝒪 is a valuation ring. For 𝒪 given as a ValuationSubring there is an instance ValuationRing A (Mathlib/RingTheory/Valuation/ValuationSubring.lean:124). Valuation rings are Bézout by the anonymous instance (priority := 100) [ValuationRing R] : IsBezout R (Mathlib/RingTheory/Valuation/ValuationRing.lean:381). IsBezout.isPrincipal_of_FG : ∀ I : Ideal R, I.FG → I.IsPrincipal is the class field (Mathlib/RingTheory/PrincipalIdealDomain.lean:67). All three were read. `IsBezout.isPrincipal_of_FG` is a field of the class `IsBezout` (Mathlib/RingTheory/PrincipalIdealDomain.lean:67), which the pinned declaration index does not list; valuation rings are Bézout in Mathlib.

items.name: Example 2.4(i): 𝒪 is coherent
items.statement: 𝒪 is coherent: that is, any finitely generated submodule of a finitely presented 𝒪-module is again finitely presented.
items.note: Deduced from the principality of finitely generated ideals. Coherence is used repeatedly: Propositions 2.10(iv) and 2.11(iv), and, implicitly, the finite presentation of M_i ∩ M′ in 2.10(iii). Mathlib has no coherent-ring notion: grep 'Coherent' in Mathlib/RingTheory finds only topological IsCoherentWith. Searched research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/*.json and research/blueprint/roadmaps/*.json. Not planned.

items.name: Example 2.4(i): the ideals I_r
items.statement: For r ∈ ℝ, r ⩾ 0, let I_r = ⋃_{ε ∈ log Γ, ε > r} π^ε 𝒪 ⊂ 𝒪.
items.note: The ideal {x : v(x) > r}. Note I_0 = 𝔪, so 𝒪/I_0 is almost zero. Not planned. Used in Theorem 2.5 and Proposition 2.11(ii).

items.name: Example 2.4(i): I_r ≈ 𝒪; nonprincipal ideals are the I_r; nonzero ideals are almost finitely presented
items.statement: For r ⩾ 0 the inclusions 𝒪 ≅ π^ε 𝒪 ⊂ I_r for ε > r show that 𝒪 ≈ I_r. However, I_r^a is not isomorphic to 𝒪^a as 𝒪^a-modules if r ∉ log Γ. All nonprincipal ideals of 𝒪 are of the form I_r; in particular all nonzero ideals I ⊂ 𝒪 satisfy I ≈ 𝒪, and hence are almost finitely presented.
items.note: Only sketched ('one can check'). Used in Proposition 2.6, which takes M = 𝒪/I for the cyclic case. Not planned.

items.name: Example 2.4(ii): ⊕ 𝒪/I_{γ_i} with γ_i → 0 is almost finitely presented
items.statement: Let γ₁, γ₂, … ∈ ℝ_{⩾0}, such that γ_i → 0 for i → ∞. Then 𝒪/I_{γ₁} ⊕ 𝒪/I_{γ₂} ⊕ ⋯ is almost finitely presented.
items.note: Stated without proof. For each ε, all but finitely many summands are killed by π^ε, and each 𝒪/I_γ ≈ 𝒪/π^{γ′} for suitable γ′ ∈ log Γ. Shows that the normal forms of Theorem 2.5 do occur. Not planned.

items.name: Theorem 2.5: classification of almost finitely generated 𝒪-modules
items.statement: Let M be any almost finitely generated 𝒪-module. Then there exists a unique sequence γ₁ ⩾ γ₂ ⩾ ⋯ ⩾ 0 of real numbers such that γ_i → 0 for i → ∞, and a unique integer r ⩾ 0 such that M ≈ 𝒪^r ⊕ 𝒪/I_{γ₁} ⊕ 𝒪/I_{γ₂} ⊕ ⋯.
items.note: Main theorem of §2. Proved on p. 15 ('This finishes the proof of the classification result') by combining Proposition 2.8(iii) (split off 𝒪^r) with Proposition 2.11(i),(ii) (torsion part, uniqueness of γ_M). It formalizes the argument of [6, §3, Theorem 8] (Faltings); acknowledgements cite [7, §9.3] (Gabber–Ramero) as inspiration. Searched research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/*.json and research/blueprint/roadmaps/*.json. Not planned.

items.name: Proposition 2.6: 𝒪 is almost noetherian
items.statement: Every almost finitely generated 𝒪-module is almost finitely presented.
items.note: Proof: cyclic case 𝒪/I via Example 2.4(i) and Proposition 2.7(iv); then filtrations with cyclic subquotients and Proposition 2.7(ii); then approximation (M ≈_ε N_ε ≈_ε L_ε gives M ≈_{2ε} L_ε). Used in §5, Lemma 5.4 (p. 40). Not planned.

items.name: Subquotients of almost finitely generated 𝒪-modules; abelian category
items.statement: Any subquotient of an almost finitely generated 𝒪-module is almost finitely generated; in particular the category of almost finitely generated 𝒪-modules is abelian.
items.note: Follows from Proposition 2.6 with Proposition 2.7(i),(iii). Used throughout §2 (Proposition 2.8(iii), torsion submodule) and in §5. Not planned.

items.name: Proposition 2.7(i) [Gabber–Ramero 2.3.18]: quotients of almost finitely generated modules
items.statement: Let 0 → M′ → M → M″ → 0 be an exact sequence of 𝒪-modules. If M is almost finitely generated, then M″ is almost finitely generated.
items.note: Cited from [8, Lemma 2.3.18] (Gabber–Ramero, Almost ring theory, LNM 1800), with no proof here. P0 does not plan almost finite generation. Not planned.

items.name: Proposition 2.7(ii) [Gabber–Ramero 2.3.18]: extensions
items.statement: Let 0 → M′ → M → M″ → 0 be an exact sequence of 𝒪-modules. If M′ and M″ are almost finitely generated (respectively presented), then M is almost finitely generated (respectively presented).
items.note: Cited from [8, Lemma 2.3.18]. Not planned.

items.name: Proposition 2.7(iii) [Gabber–Ramero 2.3.18]: kernels
items.statement: Let 0 → M′ → M → M″ → 0 be an exact sequence of 𝒪-modules. If M is almost finitely generated and M″ is almost finitely presented, then M′ is almost finitely generated.
items.note: Cited from [8, Lemma 2.3.18]. Not planned.

items.name: Proposition 2.7(iv) [Gabber–Ramero 2.3.18]: quotients by almost finitely generated submodules
items.statement: Let 0 → M′ → M → M″ → 0 be an exact sequence of 𝒪-modules. If M is almost finitely presented and M′ is almost finitely generated, then M″ is almost finitely presented.
items.note: Cited from [8, Lemma 2.3.18]. Used for the cyclic case of Proposition 2.6. Not planned.

items.name: Proposition 2.8(i): finitely generated torsion-free 𝒪-modules are free
items.statement: Let M be a finitely generated torsion-free 𝒪-module. Then M is free of finite rank.
items.note: No single Mathlib declaration, but it is a two-step consequence of Mathlib. Module.Flat.flat_iff_torsion_eq_bot_of_isBezout [IsBezout R] [IsDomain R] : Flat R M ↔ torsion R M = ⊥ (Mathlib/RingTheory/Flat/TorsionFree.lean:93) gives flatness, and Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing [Module.Finite R P] [Flat R P] : Free R P (Mathlib/RingTheory/LocalRing/Module.lean:304) gives freeness. Both were read. Marked missing because the statement itself is not a declaration. The paper's proof lifts a basis of M ⊗ κ and uses gcds in 𝒪.

items.name: Proposition 2.8(ii): almost finitely generated torsion-free modules are ≈ 𝒪^r
items.statement: Let M be an almost finitely generated torsion-free 𝒪-module. Then M ≈ 𝒪^r for a unique integer r ⩾ 0.
items.note: Proof: finitely generated submodules N_ε ⊂ M with M ≈_ε N_ε are free by (i), of rank r = dim_K(M ⊗ K). Not planned.

items.name: Proposition 2.8(iii): M ≈ 𝒪^r ⊕ N with N torsion
items.statement: Let M be an almost finitely generated 𝒪-module. Then there exists a unique integer r ⩾ 0 and an almost finitely generated torsion 𝒪-module N such that M ≈ 𝒪^r ⊕ N.
items.note: N is the torsion submodule, and r = dim_K(M ⊗ K). Only r is unique, not N. The proof uses projectivity of 𝒪^r to split approximating extensions M_ε. This reduces Theorem 2.5 to torsion modules. Not planned.

items.name: Definition 2.9: ℓ^∞(ℕ)_0, ℓ^∞_⩾(ℕ)_0 and the majorization order
items.statement: Let ℓ^∞(ℕ)_0 be the space of sequences γ = (γ₁, γ₂, …), γ_i ∈ ℝ, such that γ_i → 0 for i → ∞, endowed with the ℓ^∞-norm ‖γ‖ = max(|γ_i|). Let ℓ^∞_⩾(ℕ)_0 ⊂ ℓ^∞(ℕ)_0 be the subspace of sequences with γ₁ ⩾ γ₂ ⩾ ⋯ ⩾ 0. On ℓ^∞_⩾(ℕ)_0, the majorization order is defined by γ ⩾ γ′ if and only if for all i ⩾ 1, γ₁ + ⋯ + γ_i ⩾ γ′₁ + ⋯ + γ′_i.
items.note: Mathlib has the Banach space of sequences tending to zero (c₀), as ZeroAtInftyContinuousMap on ℕ / lp-type spaces, but not the monotone cone or majorization in this form. Grep for 'majoriz' finds nothing relevant. Not planned.

items.name: ℓ^∞(ℕ)_0 is complete and ℓ^∞_⩾(ℕ)_0 is closed
items.statement: ℓ^∞(ℕ)_0 is complete for the norm ‖·‖, and ℓ^∞_⩾(ℕ)_0 ⊂ ℓ^∞(ℕ)_0 is a closed subspace.
items.note: Stated without proof. Used in Proposition 2.11(i) to take the limit of the Cauchy sequence γ_{M_ε}. Completeness of c₀ is available in Mathlib in other packaging, but not for this carrier. Not planned.

items.name: Proposition 2.10(i): elementary divisors of finitely presented torsion 𝒪-modules
items.statement: Let M be a finitely presented torsion 𝒪-module. Then there exist unique γ_{M,1} ⩾ γ_{M,2} ⩾ ⋯ ⩾ γ_{M,k} > 0, γ_{M,i} ∈ log Γ, such that M ≅ 𝒪/π^{γ_{M,1}} ⊕ 𝒪/π^{γ_{M,2}} ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ 𝒪/π^{γ_{M,k}}. The γ_{M,i} are the jumps of the function γ ↦ dim_κ((π^γ M) ⊗_𝒪 κ) on γ ⩾ 0, γ ∈ log Γ.
items.note: Proof: a presentation M = coker A with A ∈ M_k(𝒪) ∩ GL_k(K), then the Cartan decomposition over 𝒪 (see s2-fact-cartan-decomposition). Mathlib's Smith normal form (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/FreeModule/PID.lean) needs a PID, and 𝒪 is not noetherian here. Not planned.

items.name: γ_M and the length λ(M) of a finitely presented torsion module
items.statement: For M a finitely presented torsion 𝒪-module, write γ_M = (γ_{M,1}, …, γ_{M,k}, 0, …) ∈ ℓ^∞_⩾(ℕ)_0, and set λ(M) = γ_{M,1} + ⋯ + γ_{M,k}, called the length of M (this conflicts with the standard commutative-algebra meaning of 'length').
items.note: In the proof of 2.10(iii), λ(M) = v(det A) for a presentation matrix A, i.e. the valuation of the 0th Fitting ideal. Not planned.

items.name: Cartan decomposition over 𝒪
items.statement: M_k(𝒪) ∩ GL_k(K) = ⋃ GL_k(𝒪) diag(π^{γ₁}, …, π^{γ_k}) GL_k(𝒪), the union over γ₁ ⩾ ⋯ ⩾ γ_k ⩾ 0 in log Γ. It is proved by taking π^{γ_k} to be the greatest common divisor of all entries, moving it to the lower right corner, clearing the last row and column, and inducting on k.
items.note: An unnumbered fact that the proof uses ('holds true over K with the usual proof'). The printed display omits the index set of the union. Mathlib has Smith normal form only over PIDs (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/FreeModule/PID.lean, smithNormalForm), and has none for Bézout or valuation rings. Not planned.

items.name: Duality M ↦ Hom_𝒪(M, K/𝒪) on finitely presented torsion modules
items.statement: The functor M ↦ Hom_𝒪(M, K/𝒪) exchanges submodules and quotients of finitely presented torsion 𝒪-modules and preserves the elementary divisors (Hom_𝒪(𝒪/π^γ, K/𝒪) ≅ 𝒪/π^γ).
items.note: Used, without proof, to reduce the submodule case to the quotient case in 2.10(ii). In 2.11(v) it is applied to almost finitely generated modules, which are not necessarily finitely presented; the paper treats this step tersely, and the first case also has a direct proof by the same π^ε argument. Not planned.

items.name: Proposition 2.10(ii): elementary divisors decrease under subquotients (finitely presented case)
items.statement: Let M, M′ be finitely presented torsion 𝒪-modules. If M′ is a subquotient of M, then γ_{M′,i} ⩽ γ_{M,i} for all i ⩾ 1.
items.note: Proof: reduce to quotients by duality, reduce modulo π^γ, and split a direct summand (𝒪/π^γ)^i. Not planned.

items.name: Proposition 2.10(iii): additivity of λ and majorization inequality (finitely presented case)
items.statement: Let 0 → M′ → M → M″ → 0 be an exact sequence of finitely presented torsion 𝒪-modules. Then λ(M) = λ(M′) + λ(M″) and γ_M ⩽ γ_{M′} + γ_{M″}, using the majorization order.
items.note: Additivity: a block upper triangular presentation, diagram (2.1), gives det A = det A′ det A″. Equivalently, multiplicativity of the 0th Fitting ideal. Majorization: apply part (ii) to M_i = ⊕_{j⩽i} 𝒪/π^{γ_{M,j}}. Not planned.

items.name: Proposition 2.10(iv): M ≈_ε M′ iff ‖γ_M − γ_{M′}‖ ⩽ ε
items.statement: Let M, M′ be finitely presented torsion 𝒪-modules. Then M ≈_ε M′ if and only if ‖γ_M − γ_{M′}‖ ⩽ ε.
items.note: Proof uses a quotient L of M with π^ε M′ ⊂ L ⊂ M′, coherence of 𝒪, and γ_{π^ε M′,i} = max(γ_{M′,i} − ε, 0). The converse is 'obvious' (diagonal maps). Not planned.

items.name: Elementary divisors of π^ε M
items.statement: For a finitely presented (and, by the classification, almost finitely generated) torsion 𝒪-module M and ε > 0, ε ∈ log Γ: γ_{π^ε M, i} = max(γ_{M,i} − ε, 0).
items.note: An unnumbered fact that the proofs use. For finitely presented M it is immediate from 2.10(i). For almost finitely generated M it follows from 2.11(ii). Not planned.

items.name: Proposition 2.11(i): elementary divisors of almost finitely generated torsion modules
items.statement: There exists a unique map sending any almost finitely generated torsion 𝒪-module M to an element γ_M ∈ ℓ^∞_⩾(ℕ)_0 that extends the definition for finitely presented M, and such that whenever M ≈_ε M′, then ‖γ_M − γ_{M′}‖ ⩽ ε. Set λ(M) = Σ_{i=1}^∞ γ_{M,i} ∈ ℝ_{⩾0} ∪ {∞}. γ_M = (γ_{M,1}, γ_{M,2}, …) is called the sequence of elementary divisors of M.
items.note: γ_M is defined as the limit of γ_{M_ε} for finitely presented torsion M_ε ≈_ε M. This is a Cauchy sequence by 2.10(iv), and the limit exists by completeness (Definition 2.9). Not planned.

items.name: Proposition 2.11(ii): normal form of almost finitely generated torsion modules
items.statement: Any almost finitely generated torsion 𝒪-module M with γ_M = (γ₁, γ₂, …) satisfies M ≈ 𝒪/I_{γ₁} ⊕ 𝒪/I_{γ₂} ⊕ ⋯. In particular, γ_M = 0 if and only if M is almost zero.
items.note: Proof: N_ε ≈_{2ε} M_ε by 2.10(iv), hence N ≈_{4ε} M. Not planned.

items.name: Proposition 2.11(iii): elementary divisors decrease under subquotients
items.statement: If M, M′ are almost finitely generated torsion 𝒪-modules such that M′ is a subquotient of M, then γ_{M′,i} ⩽ γ_{M,i} for all i ⩾ 1.
items.note: Proved by approximation from 2.10(ii). Not planned.

items.name: Proposition 2.11(iv): majorization and additivity of λ
items.statement: If 0 → M′ → M → M″ → 0 is an exact sequence of almost finitely generated torsion 𝒪-modules, then γ_M ⩽ γ_{M′} + γ_{M″} in the majorization order, and λ(M) = λ(M′) + λ(M″).
items.note: Proof of the reverse inequality: use finitely presented subquotients with large λ, coherence of 𝒪, and additivity in the finitely presented case. Not planned.

items.name: Proposition 2.11(v): equality of elementary divisors forces almost vanishing
items.statement: If 0 → M′ → M → M″ → 0 is an exact sequence of almost finitely generated torsion 𝒪-modules and γ_{M′} = γ_M, then M″ is almost zero. Similarly, if γ_M = γ_{M″}, then M′ is almost zero.
items.note: Proof: reduce to the second case by K/𝒪-duality, use additivity when λ(M) < ∞, and in general pass to π^ε M, which has finite length. Used in Lemma 2.12 to identify M′₁^a = M₁^a and M′_k^a = M_k^a. Not planned.

items.name: Lemma 2.12: compatible Frobenius systems of almost finitely generated O/π^k-modules are almost free
items.statement: Assume additionally that K is an algebraically closed field of characteristic p. Let M_k be an 𝒪/π^k-module for any k ⩾ 1, such that: (i) M₁ is almost finitely generated; (ii) there are maps p_k : M_{k+1} → M_k and q_k : M_k → M_{k+1} such that p_k q_k : M_k → M_k is multiplication by π, and such that M₁ →^{q_k⋯q₁} M_{k+1} →^{p_k} M_k is exact in the middle; (iii) there are isomorphisms φ_k : M_k ⊗_{𝒪/π^k, φ} 𝒪/π^{pk} ≅ M_{pk} compatible with p_k, q_k. Then there exists some integer r ⩾ 0 and isomorphisms of 𝒪^a-modules M_k^a ≅ (𝒪^a/π^k)^r for all k, such that p_k is carried to the obvious projection, q_k is carried to the multiplication-by-π morphism, and φ_k is carried to the coordinatewise Frobenius map.
items.note: This is the application of the classification used in §5. Lemma 5.11 (p. 44) checks its hypotheses via Lemma 5.9 to prove Theorem 5.1 ('Lemma 5.9 implies that the M_k satisfy the hypotheses of Lemma 2.12'). The proof uses γ_{M_k} = kγ_{M₁}, Proposition 2.11(v), flatness via [17, Lemma 5.3(i)], Lemma 2.13, and triviality of étale φ-modules over K. Not planned.

items.name: Lemma 2.13: almost finite generation lifts from A/π to π-adically complete A
items.statement: Let A be an 𝒪^a-module such that A ≅ lim←_k A/π^k, and such that A/π is almost finitely generated. Then A is almost finitely generated.
items.note: Planned: PerfectoidSpaces:P0/adic-almost-projective-modules (PerfectoidSpaces--P0 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PerfectoidSpaces--P0.json, merged before this extraction. Proof: lift a map 𝒪^r → A/π with cokernel killed by π^ε, and sum a π-adically convergent series. Used inside the proof of Lemma 2.12. Mathlib has no almost modules.

items.name: Étale φ-modules over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p are trivial
items.statement: Over any ring R of characteristic p, (finite) locally free R-modules N with an isomorphism N ⊗_{R,φ} R ≅ N are equivalent to étale 𝔽_p-local systems over R; as K is algebraically closed, these are all trivial, so (M ⊗ K, φ) ≅ (K^r, φ) for some r ⩾ 0.
items.note: An unnumbered fact the proof uses (Katz / Lang's theorem for GL_r). Searched research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/*.json and research/blueprint/roadmaps/*.json for 'φ-module'. Searches of Mathlib/Tau Ceti for a Lang-type triviality of Frobenius-semilinear automorphisms over algebraically closed fields found nothing. Not planned.

items.name: Flatness of M^a from π^k-exact sequences
items.statement: If M = lim←_k M_k and 0 → M^a →^{π^k} M^a → M_k^a → 0 is exact for all k, then M^a is flat.
items.note: Cited from [17, Lemma 5.3(i)] (Scholze, Perfectoid spaces), together with left-exactness of X ↦ X_∗. PerfectoidSpaces:P0 plans 'almost-flat' modules generally but not this criterion. Marked missing.

items.name: Pro-objects of a category
items.statement: Let C be a category, and let Ĉ = Funct(C, Set)^op, with the fully faithful embedding C → Ĉ, be its Yoneda completion. The category pro-C of pro-objects of C is the full subcategory of those objects of Ĉ which are small cofiltered inverse limits of representable objects.
items.note: DiamondsAndVStacks:D0 plans it: 'Implement pro-categories of the small categories needed for these limits and compare with the existing categorical limit API.' Mathlib has no pro-category. Searched for pro-object and ProObject: the only hit is Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Galois/Prorepresentability.lean, which is about pro-representability of fibre functors, not a pro-category. Mathlib has the dual Ind-construction only. The paper cites SGA 4 I, 8 for details. The paper uses this as the carrier category of X_profét and X_proét.

items.name: Pro-objects as formal cofiltered systems
items.statement: The category pro-C is equivalent to the category whose objects are functors F : I → C from small cofiltered index categories I and whose morphisms are given by Hom(F, G) = lim_{←J} lim_{→I} Hom(F(i), G(j)), for any F : I → C and G : J → C.
items.note: Standard (SGA 4 I, 8); stated without proof. D0 plans pro-categories and their comparison with the categorical limit API ('Implement pro-categories ... and compare with the existing categorical limit API'). From here on the paper uses this description and calls F a 'formal cofiltered inverse system F_i, i ∈ I'.

items.name: Cofiltered limits exist in pro-C
items.statement: Cofiltered inverse limits exist in pro-C (dual of SGA 4 I, Proposition 8.5.1): a double inverse system is combined into a single inverse system.
items.note: An unnumbered fact the paper uses all the time: the pro-étale presentation U = lim U_i in Definition 3.9 is formed in pro-X_ét with U_i themselves pro-objects, and it is used in Lemma 3.10(vi),(vii) and Lemma 4.6. D0 says 'compare with the existing categorical limit API'.

items.name: Locally noetherian adic space
items.statement: An adic space is called locally noetherian if it is locally of the form Spa(A, A⁺), where A is strongly noetherian, or A admits a noetherian ring of definition. As a consequence, if Y → X is étale, then locally, Y is connected.
items.note: Planned: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space (AdicSpacesPartII packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/AdicSpacesPartII.json, merged before this extraction. This is the standing hypothesis on X throughout §§3–4, recalled from Huber [9]. The consequence (locally only finitely many connected components) is the 'most nonformal' input to Lemma 3.10(vii); see the remark after its proof on p. 23. Tau Ceti has Huber pairs and Spa (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Spa/*) but no strongly noetherian or glued adic spaces. Searched Mathlib and Tau Ceti at the pinned commit: Tau Ceti's adic-space library stops at Spa of Huber pairs, rational subsets and the structure presheaf (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/**). It has no adic spaces as glued objects, no étale or finite étale morphisms of adic spaces, no pro-objects and no perfectoid spaces. Mathlib's pro-étale site (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Proetale.lean:52–67) is the Bhatt–Scholze site of schemes weakly étale over a base with fpqc covers. It is a different site from Scholze's category of pro-objects of X_ét, and Mathlib has nothing for adic spaces.

items.name: Underlying topological space of a pro-object
items.statement: For U = lim_← U_i ∈ pro-X_fét (respectively U = lim_← U_i → X in pro-X_ét) one sets |U| = lim_← |U_i|, the inverse limit of the underlying topological spaces.
items.note: Planned: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-morphism (AdicEtaleGeometry packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/AdicEtaleGeometry.json, merged before this extraction. This lets the covering conditions and Lemma 3.10(i),(iii),(iv), Proposition 3.12(iv)–(vi) be stated topologically. No pro-object of adic spaces exists in either library. Searched Mathlib and Tau Ceti at the pinned commit: Tau Ceti's adic-space library stops at Spa of Huber pairs, rational subsets and the structure presheaf (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/**). It has no adic spaces as glued objects, no étale or finite étale morphisms of adic spaces, no pro-objects and no perfectoid spaces. Mathlib's pro-étale site (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Proetale.lean:52–67) is the Bhatt–Scholze site of schemes weakly étale over a base with fpqc covers. It is a different site from Scholze's category of pro-objects of X_ét, and Mathlib has nothing for adic spaces.

items.name: Pro-finite étale site X_profét (corrected covers)
items.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian scheme or locally noetherian adic space and X_fét the category of spaces finite étale over X. The pro-finite étale site X_profét has as underlying category the category pro-X_fét. A covering is given by a family of morphisms {f_i : U_i → U} such that |U| = ⋃_i f_i(|U_i|) and such that each U_i → U can be written as an inverse limit U_i = lim_{μ<λ} U_μ → U of U_μ ∈ pro-X_fét with U_0 = U, where the limit is along the set of ordinals μ less than some ordinal λ, with the following property: for all μ < λ, U_μ → U_{<μ} := lim_{μ'<μ} U_{μ'} is the pullback of a finite étale and surjective map in X_fét. [Corrected per the 2016 corrigendum; the published text required only that the f_i be open morphisms.]
items.note: CORRECTED statement. The published version asks only that the f_i be open and jointly surjective. The corrigendum replaces openness by the transfinite-tower condition and says 'for countable limits, the definitions are unchanged', and that the underlying category is unchanged. AdicEtaleGeometry:A1 says: 'For the pro-étale extension use Scholze's corrected covering definition: arbitrary transfinite towers whose successor-to-previous-limit maps are pullbacks of finite étale surjections; the countable case is unchanged. An arbitrary open surjection of profinite sets need not split.' It also says: 'Construct the small étale and finite étale categories and their topologies'. A1 covers analytic adic spaces only; the scheme case of the paper is not planned there. Used in Proposition 3.5, Lemma 3.11 and Proposition 3.13.

items.name: The site G-fsets
items.statement: For a profinite group G, let G-fsets denote the site whose underlying category is the category of finite sets S with continuous G-action; a covering is given by a family of G-equivariant maps {f_i : S_i → S} such that S = ⋃_i f_i(S_i).
items.note: Planned: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/profinite-g-sets-site (AdicEtaleGeometry packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/AdicEtaleGeometry.json, merged before this extraction. The corrigendum does not change this part: finite sets need no transfinite condition. Mathlib has profinite groups and continuous actions, but no site of finite continuous G-sets (searched Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Galois, Mathlib/Topology/Category/Profinite). Via X_fét ≅ π₁(X, x̄)-fsets it is used for Proposition 3.5.

items.name: The site G-pfsets (corrected covers)
items.statement: For a profinite group G, let G-pfsets denote the site whose underlying category is the category of profinite sets S with continuous G-action, and a covering is given by a family of continuous G-equivariant maps {f_i : S_i → S} such that S = ⋃_i f_i(S_i) and such that each S_i → S can be written as S_i = lim_{μ<λ} S_μ → S (limit along the ordinals μ less than some ordinal λ, S_0 = S) where for all μ < λ the map S_μ → S_{<μ} := lim_{μ'<μ} S_{μ'} is the pullback of a surjective map in G-fsets. [Corrected per the 2016 corrigendum; the published text required the f_i to be open.] In particular, for any profinite group G the map G → ∗ is a covering, and more generally G → G/G' is a covering for any closed subgroup G' ⊂ G.
items.note: Planned: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/profinite-g-sets-site (AdicEtaleGeometry packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/AdicEtaleGeometry.json, merged before this extraction. CORRECTED statement. The published definition asks for 'a family of open continuous G-equivariant maps'. The corrigendum says 'A similar condition should then also appear ... in the definition of covers in Definition 3.4'. The last sentence of the statement is the corrigendum's remark: embed G into ∏_{μ<λ} H_μ of finite groups and let G_μ be the image in ∏_{μ'≤μ} H_{μ'}. That remark is what keeps Proposition 3.7(iii), which uses the cover G → pt, valid. No site of profinite G-sets exists in Mathlib or Tau Ceti. A1 plans only the geometric side.

items.name: Profinite G-sets are pro-(finite G-sets)
items.statement: Every profinite set with continuous action by a profinite group G is an inverse limit of finite sets with continuous G-action; this identifies G-pfsets ≅ pro-(G-fsets) as categories.
items.note: Planned: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/profinite-g-sets-site (AdicEtaleGeometry packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/AdicEtaleGeometry.json, merged before this extraction. An unnumbered fact used to deduce the categorical part of Proposition 3.5 from X_fét ≅ π₁(X, x̄)-fsets. Mathlib has the version without an action, Profinite.asLimit (Mathlib/Topology/Category/Profinite/AsLimit.lean:94: a profinite space is the limit of its finite discrete quotients). It has no G-equivariant version and no pro-category.

items.name: X_profét ≅ π₁(X, x̄)-pfsets
items.statement: Let X be a connected locally noetherian scheme or connected locally noetherian adic space, with geometric base point x̄. Then there is a canonical equivalence of sites X_profét ≅ π₁(X, x̄)-pfsets, given by sending Y = lim_← Y_i → X to S(Y) = lim_← S_i, where S_i is the fibre of x̄ in Y_i. (Both sites are taken with the corrected coverings of Definitions 3.3 and 3.4.)
items.note: Planned: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/profinite-etale-galois-sets (AdicEtaleGeometry packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/AdicEtaleGeometry.json, merged before this extraction. The corrigendum restricts the coverings on both sides in the same way: pullbacks of finite étale surjections correspond to pullbacks of surjections of finite π₁-sets. So the equivalence of sites survives, and the covering comparison becomes formal. The printed proof instead shows that Y → Z is open iff S(Y) → S(Z) is open, via Lemma 3.6. It needs the finite étale fundamental group X_fét ≅ π₁(X, x̄)-fsets, which neither library has for schemes or adic spaces (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Galois has the abstract Galois-category formalism but no étale fundamental group of a scheme). Used in Lemma 3.11 and Proposition 3.13.

items.name: Structure of open surjections in G-pfsets
items.statement: Let S → S' be an open surjective map in G-pfsets for a profinite group G. Then S → S' can be written as an inverse limit S = lim_← T_i → S', where each T_i is of the form T_i = A_i ×_{B_i} S', where A_i → B_i is a surjection in G-fsets, and S' → B_i is some surjective map. Moreover, one can assume that S = lim_← A_i and S' = lim_← B_i.
items.note: Planned: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/open-surjection-profinite-structure (AdicEtaleGeometry packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/AdicEtaleGeometry.json, merged before this extraction. The corrigendum leaves this lemma unchanged: it is a cofiltered (not transfinite) presentation. The corrigendum explains that deducing a splitting from it (the original proof of Proposition 3.7(i)) is the error. It is used for the openness comparison in Proposition 3.5 and in Lemma 3.11. Nothing in Mathlib.

items.name: The sheaf F_M of continuous maps
items.statement: Let M be any topological G-module. The sheaf F_M on G-pfsets is defined by F_M(S) = Hom_{cont,G}(S, M). It is a sheaf: the covering maps are open, so the continuity condition glues.
items.note: Planned: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/profinite-g-sets-site (AdicEtaleGeometry packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/AdicEtaleGeometry.json, merged before this extraction. With the corrected coverings, the covering maps are still open (surjections of profinite sets with finite-set-pullback steps), so the gluing argument survives. This gives the site-theoretic interpretation of continuous group cohomology in Proposition 3.7(iii). Mathlib has continuous cohomology (continuousCohomology, Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/Basic.lean:131) but no site G-pfsets.

items.name: Splitting of transfinite towers of finite surjections (corrected Prop. 3.7(i))
items.statement: Let S → S' be a map of profinite sets such that S = lim_{μ<λ} S_μ, with S_0 = S', having the property that S_μ → S_{<μ} := lim_{μ'<μ} S_{μ'} is the pullback of a surjective map of finite sets for all μ < λ. Then S → S' admits a continuous splitting. [This replaces the published Proposition 3.7(i), 'Any continuous open surjective map S → S' of profinite sets admits a continuous splitting', which is false.]
items.note: Planned: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/transfinite-tower-splitting (AdicEtaleGeometry packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/AdicEtaleGeometry.json, merged before this extraction. CORRECTED statement. The published claim is false: the corrigendum cites Ribes–Zalesskii, Profinite groups, 2nd ed., Example 5.6.9, whose counterexample uses uncountable inverse limits. The correct variant 'follows directly from transfinite induction'. Countable towers (λ = ω) are allowed. It is used in the proof of (ii): S → S/G splits for a free G-action, and a cover {T_i → T} of profinite sets obtained by restricting a corrected cover splits. Mathlib has no splitting result for profinite sets.

items.name: Evaluation at free profinite G-sets is exact
items.statement: For any S ∈ G-pfsets with free G-action, the functor F ↦ F(S) on sheaves over G-pfsets is exact. (In particular any such S has the form S = T × G for a profinite set T with trivial G-action.)
items.note: Planned: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/free-g-profinite-sections-exact (AdicEtaleGeometry packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/AdicEtaleGeometry.json, merged before this extraction. Unaffected as a statement. The proof uses (i) twice. First, S → S/G splits: with the corrigendum's remark, S → S/G is a transfinite tower of free torsors under finite groups G_{<μ}/G_μ, each split over a profinite base, so the corrected (i) applies. Second, the restricted covers {T_i → T} split: pullbacks of corrected covers along T → S are again transfinite towers of pullbacks of finite surjections. Used in (iii) to get RΓ(Gⁿ, F_M) = Hom_{cont,G}(Gⁿ, M). Not in any library.

items.name: H^i(pt, F_M) = H^i_cont(G, M)
items.statement: Let G be a profinite group and M a topological G-module. We have a canonical isomorphism H^i(pt, F_M) = H^i_cont(G, M) for all i ⩾ 0. Here pt ∈ G-pfsets is the one-point set with trivial G-action.
items.note: Planned: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/profinite-g-set-cohomology (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H0 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H0.json, merged before this extraction. The proof uses the cover G → pt and the Cartan–Leray spectral sequence (SGA 4 V, Corollaire 3.3), with RΓ(Gⁿ, F_M) = Hom_{cont,G}(Gⁿ, M) = Hom_cont(Gⁿ⁻¹, M). The corrigendum confirms that G → ∗ is a corrected cover. The right-hand side exists in Mathlib: continuousCohomology (Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/Basic.lean:131, homogeneous cochains). The site, and hence the comparison, does not. Tau Ceti's ContCohomology/ContinuousCohomologyIso.lean compares cochain models, not a site.

items.name: Étale and finite étale morphisms in pro-X_ét
items.statement: A morphism U → V of objects of pro-X_ét is called étale (respectively finite étale) if it is induced by an étale (respectively finite étale) morphism U_0 → V_0 of objects in X_ét: that is, U = U_0 ×_{V_0} V via some morphism V → V_0.
items.note: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1 says: 'For the pro-étale extension use Scholze's corrected covering definition: arbitrary transfinite towers whose successor-to-previous-limit maps are pullbacks of finite étale surjections; the countable case is unchanged. An arbitrary open surjection of profinite sets need not split.' It also says: 'Construct the small étale and finite étale categories and their topologies'. A1 covers analytic adic spaces only; the scheme case of the paper is not planned there. This is part of 'the pro-étale extension'. Lemma 3.10 develops its base-change, composition and openness properties.

items.name: Pro-étale morphism and pro-étale presentation
items.statement: A morphism U → V of objects of pro-X_ét is called pro-étale if it can be written as a cofiltered inverse limit U = lim_← U_i of objects U_i → V étale over V, such that U_i → U_j is finite étale and surjective for large i > j. (Here U_i is itself a pro-object of X_ét, and the cofiltered inverse limit lim_← U_i exists in pro-X_ét.) Such a presentation U = lim_← U_i → V is called a pro-étale presentation.
items.note: The corrigendum leaves the class of pro-étale morphisms and the category X_proét unchanged; only the coverings are restricted. AdicEtaleGeometry:A1 says: 'For the pro-étale extension use Scholze's corrected covering definition: arbitrary transfinite towers whose successor-to-previous-limit maps are pullbacks of finite étale surjections; the countable case is unchanged. An arbitrary open surjection of profinite sets need not split.' It also says: 'Construct the small étale and finite étale categories and their topologies'. A1 covers analytic adic spaces only; the scheme case of the paper is not planned there.

items.name: The pro-étale site X_proét (corrected covers)
items.statement: The pro-étale site X_proét has as underlying category the full subcategory of pro-X_ét of objects that are pro-étale over X. A covering in X_proét is given by a family of pro-étale morphisms {f_i : U_i → U} such that |U| = ⋃_i f_i(|U_i|) and such that each f_i can be written as a transfinite composition U_i = lim_{μ<λ} U_μ → U_0 → U, where U_0 → U is étale, the limit runs over the ordinals μ less than some ordinal λ, and for all 0 < μ < λ the map U_μ → U_{<μ} := lim_{μ'<μ} U_{μ'} is the pullback of a finite étale and surjective map in X_ét. [Corrected per the 2016 corrigendum, which asks for 'a similar condition' to that of Definition 3.3; for countable limits the covers are unchanged.]
items.note: CORRECTED statement. The published covers are all jointly surjective families of pro-étale morphisms. The corrigendum states only that 'a similar condition should then also appear in the definition of covers in the pro-étale topology, Definition 3.9'. The étale first step U_0 → U is my reading, obtained by combining the Definition 3.3 condition with the étale-then-pro-finite-étale factorisation of pro-étale maps (Lemma 3.10(vi) proof). The assembler may prefer to state it as 'a transfinite composition of pullbacks of étale maps (first step) and finite étale surjections'. AdicEtaleGeometry:A1 says: 'For the pro-étale extension use Scholze's corrected covering definition: arbitrary transfinite towers whose successor-to-previous-limit maps are pullbacks of finite étale surjections; the countable case is unchanged. An arbitrary open surjection of profinite sets need not split.' It also says: 'Construct the small étale and finite étale categories and their topologies'. A1 covers analytic adic spaces only; the scheme case of the paper is not planned there. This is the central object of the paper (§§4–8).

items.name: Base change in pro-X_ét
items.statement: Let U, V, W ∈ pro-X_ét, and assume that U → V is étale (respectively finite étale, respectively pro-étale), and W → V is any morphism. Then U ×_V W exists in pro-X_ét, the map U ×_V W → W is étale (respectively finite étale, respectively pro-étale), and the map |U ×_V W| → |U| ×_{|V|} |W| of underlying topological spaces is surjective.
items.note: Part of 'verifies that X_proét is indeed a site' (p. 20). Stability of covers under base change is a site axiom, so this belongs to constructing the pro-étale topology in A1. The surjectivity uses the fact that inverse limits of nonempty compact spaces are nonempty. AdicEtaleGeometry:A1 says: 'For the pro-étale extension use Scholze's corrected covering definition: arbitrary transfinite towers whose successor-to-previous-limit maps are pullbacks of finite étale surjections; the countable case is unchanged. An arbitrary open surjection of profinite sets need not split.' It also says: 'Construct the small étale and finite étale categories and their topologies'. A1 covers analytic adic spaces only; the scheme case of the paper is not planned there.

items.name: Composition of étale maps in pro-X_ét
items.statement: A composition U → V → W of two étale (respectively finite étale) morphisms in pro-X_ét is étale (respectively finite étale).
items.note: Composition of covers is a site axiom; this is part of the verification that X_proét is a site. AdicEtaleGeometry:A1 says: 'For the pro-étale extension use Scholze's corrected covering definition: arbitrary transfinite towers whose successor-to-previous-limit maps are pullbacks of finite étale surjections; the countable case is unchanged. An arbitrary open surjection of profinite sets need not split.' It also says: 'Construct the small étale and finite étale categories and their topologies'. A1 covers analytic adic spaces only; the scheme case of the paper is not planned there.

items.name: Quasicompact opens of |U| are étale subobjects
items.statement: Let U ∈ pro-X_ét and let W ⊂ |U| be a quasicompact open subset. Then there is some V ∈ pro-X_ét with an étale map V → U such that |V| → |U| induces a homeomorphism |V| ≅ W. If U ∈ X_proét, the following strengthening is true: one can take V ∈ X_proét, and for any V' ∈ X_proét such that V' → U factors over |W| on topological spaces, the map V' → U factors over V.
items.note: Planned: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-quasicompact-opens (AdicEtaleGeometry packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/AdicEtaleGeometry.json, merged before this extraction. Used in (iv), in Proposition 3.12 (covering by 'open subsets U_i ⊂ U'), and in Definition 4.3(ii): quasicompact opens of U give objects of X_proét. A1's text does not name it. Searched Mathlib and Tau Ceti at the pinned commit: Tau Ceti's adic-space library stops at Spa of Huber pairs, rational subsets and the structure presheaf (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/**). It has no adic spaces as glued objects, no étale or finite étale morphisms of adic spaces, no pro-objects and no perfectoid spaces. Mathlib's pro-étale site (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Proetale.lean:52–67) is the Bhatt–Scholze site of schemes weakly étale over a base with fpqc covers. It is a different site from Scholze's category of pro-objects of X_ét, and Mathlib has nothing for adic spaces.

items.name: Pro-étale maps are open
items.statement: Any pro-étale map U → V in pro-X_ét is open.
items.note: Planned: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-maps-open (AdicEtaleGeometry packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/AdicEtaleGeometry.json, merged before this extraction. The proof reduces to openness of étale maps (Huber [9, Proposition 1.7.8] in the adic case). It is used for Lemma 3.11, Proposition 3.12(i), and the observation that corrected covers are open. A1 plans 'Establish open images' for étale morphisms of adic spaces, not this pro-object statement.

items.name: Surjective (finite) étale maps come from a finite level
items.statement: A surjective étale (respectively surjective finite étale) map U → V in pro-X_ét with V ∈ X_proét comes via pullback along V → V_0 from a surjective étale (respectively surjective finite étale) map U_0 → V_0 of objects U_0, V_0 ∈ X_ét.
items.note: Planned: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-surjective-etale-descent (AdicEtaleGeometry packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/AdicEtaleGeometry.json, merged before this extraction. Used in Lemma 3.16's reduction to étale covers. Searched Mathlib and Tau Ceti at the pinned commit: Tau Ceti's adic-space library stops at Spa of Huber pairs, rational subsets and the structure presheaf (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/**). It has no adic spaces as glued objects, no étale or finite étale morphisms of adic spaces, no pro-objects and no perfectoid spaces. Mathlib's pro-étale site (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Proetale.lean:52–67) is the Bhatt–Scholze site of schemes weakly étale over a base with fpqc covers. It is a different site from Scholze's category of pro-objects of X_ét, and Mathlib has nothing for adic spaces.

items.name: Composition of pro-étale maps
items.statement: Let U → V → W be pro-étale morphisms in pro-X_ét, and assume that W ∈ X_proét. Then U, V ∈ X_proét and the composition U → W is pro-étale.
items.note: A site axiom. The proof factors a pro-étale map as an étale map followed by an inverse system of finite étale surjections, and reduces to 'a simple exercise in X_profét'. AdicEtaleGeometry:A1 says: 'For the pro-étale extension use Scholze's corrected covering definition: arbitrary transfinite towers whose successor-to-previous-limit maps are pullbacks of finite étale surjections; the countable case is unchanged. An arbitrary open surjection of profinite sets need not split.' It also says: 'Construct the small étale and finite étale categories and their topologies'. A1 covers analytic adic spaces only; the scheme case of the paper is not planned there.

items.name: Finite projective limits in X_proét
items.statement: Arbitrary finite projective limits exist in X_proét.
items.note: The 'most nonformal part': the equalizer case needs that any U ∈ X_ét has locally only finitely many connected components, which is where the locally noetherian hypothesis is used. AdicEtaleGeometry:A1 says: 'For the pro-étale extension use Scholze's corrected covering definition: arbitrary transfinite towers whose successor-to-previous-limit maps are pullbacks of finite étale surjections; the countable case is unchanged. An arbitrary open surjection of profinite sets need not split.' It also says: 'Construct the small étale and finite étale categories and their topologies'. A1 covers analytic adic spaces only; the scheme case of the paper is not planned there.

items.name: X_profét inside X_proét
items.statement: Under the fully faithful embedding of categories X_profét ⊂ X_proét, a morphism f : U → V in X_profét is open if and only if it is pro-étale as a morphism in X_proét. In particular, the notions of coverings coincide, and there is a map of sites X_proét → X_profét.
items.note: Planned: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-profinite-etale-morphism-of-sites (AdicEtaleGeometry packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/AdicEtaleGeometry.json, merged before this extraction. With the corrected covers (Definitions 3.3 and 3.9), 'the notions of coverings coincide' holds directly: both are jointly surjective families of transfinite towers of pullbacks of finite étale surjections. The open ⇔ pro-étale statement for morphisms is unaffected and follows from Lemma 3.6 and Proposition 3.5. Used in the proof of Proposition 3.13. Searched Mathlib and Tau Ceti at the pinned commit: Tau Ceti's adic-space library stops at Spa of Huber pairs, rational subsets and the structure presheaf (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/**). It has no adic spaces as glued objects, no étale or finite étale morphisms of adic spaces, no pro-objects and no perfectoid spaces. Mathlib's pro-étale site (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Proetale.lean:52–67) is the Bhatt–Scholze site of schemes weakly étale over a base with fpqc covers. It is a different site from Scholze's category of pro-objects of X_ét, and Mathlib has nothing for adic spaces.

items.name: Pro-affinoid objects are quasicompact
items.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian scheme or locally noetherian adic space. Let U = lim_← U_i → X be a pro-étale presentation of U ∈ X_proét, such that all U_i are affinoid. Then U is a quasicompact object of X_proét.

items.name: Pullback to profinite étale sites of points
items.statement: Let x ∈ X, corresponding to a map Y = Spa(K, K⁺) → X (respectively Y = Spec(K) → X) into X. (In the case of adic spaces, the image of Y may be larger than x itself.) Then there is a morphism of topoi i_x : Y_profét~ → X_proét~, such that the pullback of F ∈ X_proét~ is the sheafification i_x^* F of the functor V ↦ lim_{→ V→U} F(U), where U ∈ X_proét, and V → U is a map compatible with the projections to Y → X.

items.name: The object X_L ∈ X_proét

Let X_L = X ×_{Spec K} Spec L (respectively X_L = X ×_{Spa(K,K⁺)} Spa(L, L⁺)). One also defines an object of X_proét, denoted by the same symbol X_L, as the formal inverse limit of the X_{L_i} ∈ X_ét where L_i ⊂ L runs through the finite extensions of K.

items.name: Exactness of inverse limits on a site
items.statement: Let F_i, i ∈ ℕ, be an inverse system of abelian sheaves on a site T. Assume that there is a basis B for the site T, such that for any U ∈ B, the following two conditions hold: (i) the higher inverse limit R¹lim_← F_i(U) = 0 vanishes; (ii) all cohomology groups H^j(U, F_i) = 0 vanish for j > 0. Then R^j lim_← F_i = 0 for j > 0 and (lim_← F_i)(U) = lim_← F_i(U) for all U ∈ T. Moreover, H^j(U, lim_← F_i) = 0 for U ∈ B and j > 0.

items.name: Standing setup: X over a perfectoid field K
items.statement: K is a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 with an open and bounded valuation subring K⁺ ⊂ K, and X over Spa(K, K⁺) is a locally noetherian adic space. Write Γ = |K^×| ⊂ ℝ_{>0}, identify ℝ_{>0} with ℝ using the logarithm with base |p|, and for r ∈ log Γ choose p^r ∈ K with |p^r| = |p|^r.

items.name: Affinoid perfectoid object of X_proét
items.statement: Let U ∈ X_proét (X locally noetherian over Spa(K, K⁺), K perfectoid). We say that U is affinoid perfectoid if U has a pro-étale presentation U = lim_← U_i → X by affinoid U_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺) such that, denoting by R⁺ the p-adic completion of lim_→ R_i⁺, and R = R⁺[p⁻¹], the pair (R, R⁺) is a perfectoid affinoid (K, K⁺)-algebra.

items.name: The functor U ↦ Û
items.statement: With an affinoid perfectoid U ∈ X_proét as in Definition 4.3(i), one associates Û = Spa(R, R⁺), an affinoid perfectoid space over K. It is well defined (independent of the pro-étale presentation U = lim_← U_i), U ↦ Û defines a functor from affinoid perfectoid U ∈ X_proét to affinoid perfectoid spaces over K, and if U = lim_← U_i is a pro-étale presentation then Û ∼ lim_← U_i in the sense of [17] (Scholze, Perfectoid spaces, Definition 7.14); in particular |Û| = |U|. By Lemma 4.5 it is compatible with open embeddings and extends to a functor U ↦ Û from perfectoid U ∈ X_proét to perfectoid spaces over K.

items.name: Étale maps preserve affinoid perfectoid
items.statement: Let U = lim_← U_i ∈ X_proét, U_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺), be affinoid perfectoid, with a pro-étale presentation. Let (R, R⁺) be the completion of the direct limit of the (R_i, R_i⁺), so that Û = Spa(R, R⁺). Assume that V_i = Spa(S_i, S_i⁺) → U_i is an étale map which can be written as a composition of rational subsets and finite étale maps. For j ⩾ i, write V_j = V_i ×_{U_i} U_j = Spa(S_j, S_j⁺), and V = V_i ×_{U_i} U = lim_← V_j ∈ X_proét. Let A_j be the p-adic completion of the p-torsion-free quotient of S_j⁺ ⊗_{R_j⁺} R⁺. Then the completion (S, S⁺) of the direct limit of the (S_j, S_j⁺) is a perfectoid affinoid (K, K⁺)-algebra. In particular, V is affinoid perfectoid. Moreover, V̂ = V_j ×_{U_j} Û in the category of adic spaces over K, and S = A_j[1/p] for any j ⩾ i.

items.name: Connected affinoids are K(π,1) for p-torsion coefficients
items.statement: Let X = Spa(A, A⁺) be an affinoid connected noetherian adic space over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p).
