items.name: Perfectoid U give perfectoid spaces
items.statement: For any perfectoid U ∈ X_proét, (|U|, Ô_X||U|, (|•(x)| | x ∈ |U|)) is an adic, in fact perfectoid, space, given by Û. (Remark 4.11: this gives a base of the topology on which Ô_X⁺ and Ô_X behave as expected.)
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/completed-structure-sheaf-on-affinoid-perfectoids (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Remark 4.11 asserts such a base exists for all locally noetherian adic spaces over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) 'by Proposition 3.15', meaning Proposition 4.8 together with Proposition 3.15. Searched Mathlib and Tau Ceti at the pinned commit: Tau Ceti's adic-space library stops at Spa of Huber pairs, rational subsets and the structure presheaf (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/**). It has no adic spaces as glued objects, no étale or finite étale morphisms of adic spaces, no pro-objects and no perfectoid spaces. Mathlib's pro-étale site (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Proetale.lean:52–67) is the Bhatt–Scholze site of schemes weakly étale over a base with fpqc covers. It is a different site from Scholze's category of pro-objects of X_ét, and Mathlib has nothing for adic spaces.

items.name: H^i(U, 𝕃 ⊗ O_X⁺/p)^a on affinoid perfectoids
items.statement: In the situation of Lemma 4.10 (U ∈ X_proét affinoid perfectoid, Û = Spa(R, R⁺)), assume that 𝕃 is an 𝔽_p-local system on X_ét. Then for all i > 0, the cohomology group H^i(U, 𝕃 ⊗ O_X⁺/p)^a is almost zero, and for i = 0 it is an almost finitely generated projective R⁺ᵃ/p-module M(U). If U' ∈ X_proét is affinoid perfectoid, corresponding to Û' = Spa(R', R'⁺), and U' → U is some map in X_proét, then M(U') = M(U) ⊗_{R⁺ᵃ/p} R'⁺ᵃ/p.
items.note: The proof trivializes 𝕃 on a finite étale Galois cover, then uses almost purity and almost faithfully flat descent (Gabber–Ramero [8, Section 3.4]). It is used in §5 for the primitive comparison theorem. Searched Mathlib and Tau Ceti at the pinned commit: Tau Ceti's adic-space library stops at Spa of Huber pairs, rational subsets and the structure presheaf (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/**). It has no adic spaces as glued objects, no étale or finite étale morphisms of adic spaces, no pro-objects and no perfectoid spaces. Mathlib's pro-étale site (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Proetale.lean:52–67) is the Bhatt–Scholze site of schemes weakly étale over a base with fpqc covers. It is a different site from Scholze's category of pro-objects of X_ét, and Mathlib has nothing for adic spaces.

items.name: Finiteness of F_p-étale cohomology of proper smooth adic spaces
items.statement: Let K be an algebraically closed complete extension of ℚ_p with an open and bounded valuation subring K⁺ ⊂ K, let X be a proper smooth adic space over Spa(K, K⁺), and let 𝕃 be an 𝔽_p-local system on X_ét. Then H^i(X_ét, 𝕃) is a finite-dimensional 𝔽_p-vector space for all i ⩾ 0.
items.note: No atlas stage plans the primitive comparison theorem or the finiteness of F_p-étale cohomology of proper smooth adic spaces over C; the PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-18 extraction (item 085) records the same absence. ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H0–H3 plan classical étale cohomology (ℓ-adic, curves), not this theorem. Searched atlas roadmaps for 'primitive comparison', 'finiteness', 'proper smooth adic space'; Mathlib and Tau Ceti have no étale cohomology of adic spaces (Tau Ceti AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace covers only Spa, valuation spectra and Huber rings). Proof (p. 46–47): reduce to X′ = X ×_{Spa(K,K⁺)} Spa(K, O_K); Lemma 5.9 plus Lemma 2.12 give H^i(X_proét, 𝕃 ⊗ Ô^+_{X♭})^a ≅ (O^a_{K♭})^r Frobenius-equivariantly; the Artin–Schreier sequence then gives H^i(X_ét, 𝕃) ≅ 𝔽_p^r. This is the paper's main input for the de Rham comparison of §8.

items.name: Vanishing above twice the dimension
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 5.1 (K algebraically closed complete over ℚ_p, K⁺ ⊂ K open bounded valuation subring, X proper smooth over Spa(K, K⁺), 𝕃 an 𝔽_p-local system on X_ét), H^i(X_ét, 𝕃) = 0 for i > 2 dim X.
items.note: No atlas stage plans the primitive comparison theorem or the finiteness of F_p-étale cohomology of proper smooth adic spaces over C; the PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-18 extraction (item 085) records the same absence. ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H0–H3 plan classical étale cohomology (ℓ-adic, curves), not this theorem. Searched atlas roadmaps for 'primitive comparison', 'finiteness', 'proper smooth adic space'; Mathlib and Tau Ceti have no étale cohomology of adic spaces (Tau Ceti AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace covers only Spa, valuation spectra and Huber rings). Follows from the vanishing part of Lemma 5.9 via the isomorphism H^i(X_ét,𝕃) ⊗ K^{+a}/p ≅ H^i(X_ét, 𝕃 ⊗ O_X^{+a}/p) and H^i(X_ét,𝕃) ≅ 𝔽_p^r.

items.name: Primitive comparison theorem
items.statement: Let K be an algebraically closed complete extension of ℚ_p with an open and bounded valuation subring K⁺ ⊂ K, let X be a proper smooth adic space over Spa(K, K⁺), and let 𝕃 be an 𝔽_p-local system on X_ét. Then for all i ⩾ 0 there is an isomorphism of almost K⁺-modules H^i(X_ét, 𝕃) ⊗ K^{+a}/p ≅ H^i(X_ét, 𝕃 ⊗ O_X^{+a}/p).
items.note: No atlas stage plans the primitive comparison theorem or the finiteness of F_p-étale cohomology of proper smooth adic spaces over C; the PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-18 extraction (item 085) records the same absence. ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H0–H3 plan classical étale cohomology (ℓ-adic, curves), not this theorem. Searched atlas roadmaps for 'primitive comparison', 'finiteness', 'proper smooth adic space'; Mathlib and Tau Ceti have no étale cohomology of adic spaces (Tau Ceti AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace covers only Spa, valuation spectra and Huber rings). The almost setting is that of K⁺ and its ideal of topologically nilpotent elements. Proved at the end of §5 (p. 46–47) from Lemma 5.9, Lemma 2.12, Lemma 5.11, Corollary 4.7, Lemma 3.18 and the Artin–Schreier sequence. Used for Corollary 5.12 and the comparison theorems of §8.

items.name: Étale toric charts around closures of points
items.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field, let V be an affinoid smooth adic space over Spa(K, O_K), and let x ∈ V with closure M = \overline{\{x\}} ⊂ V. Then there exists a rational subset U ⊂ V containing M, together with an étale map U → 𝕋ⁿ which factors as a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps. Here, 𝕋ⁿ is as defined in Example 4.4.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/toric-charts-for-smooth-spaces (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Proof uses Huber [9, Corollary 1.6.10] (a smooth space is locally étale over a unit ball 𝔹ⁿ) and [9, Lemma 2.2.8] (an étale map is locally an open embedding followed by a finite étale map), then embeds 𝔹ⁿ in 𝕋ⁿ as {|T_i − 1| ⩽ |p|}. Used in Lemma 5.3.

items.name: Nested finite affinoid covers with toric charts
items.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field and let X be a proper smooth adic space over Spa(K, O_K). For any integer N ⩾ 1, one may find N finite covers V_i^{(1)}, …, V_i^{(N)} of X by affinoid open subsets such that: (i) for all i and k = 1, …, N − 1, the closure \overline{V}_i^{(k+1)} of V_i^{(k+1)} in X is contained in V_i^{(k)}; (ii) for all i, V_i^{(N)} ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ V_i^{(1)} is a chain of rational subsets; (iii) for all i, j, the intersection V_i^{(1)} ∩ V_j^{(1)} ⊂ V_i^{(1)} is a rational subset; (iv) for all i, there is an étale map V_i^{(1)} → 𝕋ⁿ that factors as a composite of rational subsets and finite étale maps.
items.note: Proof uses Temkin [19]: in a proper Berkovich space every point has an affinoid neighbourhood, so every \overline{\{x\}} has an affinoid open neighbourhood; then Lemma 5.2. No stage plans this covering lemma (searched AdicEtaleGeometry, AdicSpacesPartII, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology). Used in the Čech argument of Lemma 5.9.

items.name: Finiteness of images through spectral sequences
items.statement: Let K be a nondiscretely valued complete nonarchimedean field, and let E^{p,q}_{∗,(i)} ⇒ M^{p+q}_{(i)}, i = 1, …, N, be upper right quadrant spectral sequences of almost O_K-modules, together with maps of spectral sequences E^{p,q}_{∗,(i)} → E^{p,q}_{∗,(i+1)}, M^{p+q}_{(i)} → M^{p+q}_{(i+1)} for i = 1, …, N − 1. Assume that for some r, the image on the rth sheet, E^{p,q}_{r,(i)} → E^{p,q}_{r,(i+1)}, is almost finitely generated over O_K for all i, p, q. Then the image of M^k_{(1)} in M^k_{(N)} is an almost finitely generated O_K-module for k ⩽ N − 2.
items.note: Proof by induction on i = 1, …, k+2 using the abutment filtrations, Proposition 2.6 (images of almost finitely generated maps stay so on later sheets) and an exact sequence of images. Pure homological algebra over the almost ring O_K; Mathlib has spectral sequences only in rudimentary form and no almost mathematics; PerfectoidSpaces:P0 plans almost modules but not this lemma. Used in Lemma 5.6(ii) and Lemma 5.9.

items.name: Koszul complex computes continuous ℤ_pⁿ-cohomology
items.statement: If M is a topological ℤ_pⁿ-module such that M = lim_← M/p^m, with M carrying the inverse limit topology of the discrete topologies on M/p^m, then continuous ℤ_pⁿ-cohomology with values in M is computed by the Koszul complex 0 → M → Mⁿ → ⋯ → ⋀^q Mⁿ → ⋯ → Mⁿ → M → 0, where the first map is (γ_1 − 1, …, γ_n − 1).
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory's P7 packet (research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json) requests this from AInfCohomology:AI.3 for every locally noetherian adic space over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p), and AI.3's stage text owns the completed integral structure sheaf, its tilt, the Witt sheaf A_inf,X and the toric continuous-cochain computation; routed there (route 5). Unnumbered fact used in the proof of Lemma 5.5. Proof: the Koszul complex of Λ = ℤ_p[[ℤ_pⁿ]] ≅ ℤ_p[[T_1, …, T_n]] on (T_1, …, T_n) resolves ℤ_p; apply Hom_cont(−, M). Mathlib has continuousCohomology but no Koszul computation for ℤ_pⁿ; the Tau Ceti ProfiniteCohomology roadmap Layer 10 plans all-degree continuous cohomology for discrete modules, not this computation.

items.name: Continuous cohomology of the perfectoid torus
items.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field of characteristic 0 that contains all p-power roots of unity; choose a compatible system ζ_{p^ℓ} ∈ K of p^ℓth roots of unity. Let R_0 = O_K⟨T_1^{±1}, …, T_n^{±1}⟩, and R = O_K⟨T_1^{±1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{±1/p^∞}⟩. Let ℤ_pⁿ act on R, such that the kth basis vector γ_k ∈ ℤ_pⁿ acts on the basis via T_1^{i_1}⋯T_n^{i_n} ↦ ζ^{i_k} T_1^{i_1}⋯T_n^{i_n}, where ζ^{i_k} = ζ_{p^ℓ}^{i_k p^ℓ} whenever i_k p^ℓ ∈ ℤ. Then H^q_cont(ℤ_pⁿ, R/p^m) is an almost finitely presented R_0-module for all m, and the map ⋀^q R_0ⁿ = H^q_cont(ℤ_pⁿ, R_0) → H^q_cont(ℤ_pⁿ, R) is injective with cokernel killed by ζ_p − 1.
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory's P7 packet (research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json) requests this from AInfCohomology:AI.3 for every locally noetherian adic space over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p), and AI.3's stage text owns the completed integral structure sheaf, its tilt, the Witt sheaf A_inf,X and the toric continuous-cochain computation; routed there (route 5). Proof: decompose R/p^m into the ℤ_pⁿ-stable pieces R_0/p^m·T_1^{i_1}⋯T_n^{i_n}, i_k ∈ [0,1) ∩ ℤ[p^{-1}], and use the Koszul fact (separate item); a piece with i_k of denominator p^ℓ has cohomology killed by ζ_{p^ℓ} − 1. The same computation reappears in BMS1 §8; AInfCohomology:AI.3 plans 'Build a toric perfectoid cover of a small framed affine, compute its continuous group cochains', but in the A_inf setting of BMS1 over a formal model, not this almost statement mod p^m. Used in Lemma 5.6 and Proposition 6.16.

items.name: Base change for toric continuous cohomology
items.statement: In the situation of Lemma 5.5, if S_0 is a p-adically complete flat ℤ_p-algebra with the p-adic topology, then H^q_cont(ℤ_pⁿ, S_0/p^m ⊗_{R_0/p^m} R/p^m) = S_0/p^m ⊗_{R_0/p^m} H^q_cont(ℤ_pⁿ, R/p^m) for all m, and H^q_cont(ℤ_pⁿ, S_0 ⊗̂_{R_0} R) = S_0 ⊗̂_{R_0} H^q_cont(ℤ_pⁿ, R).
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory's P7 packet (research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json) requests this from AInfCohomology:AI.3 for every locally noetherian adic space over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p), and AI.3's stage text owns the completed integral structure sheaf, its tilt, the Witt sheaf A_inf,X and the toric continuous-cochain computation; routed there (route 5). Proved as 'immediate from the calculations' (explicit direct-sum decomposition). The flatness hypothesis is stated for S_0 over ℤ_p; the application (proof of Lemma 5.6(ii)) uses S_m^{(j)+} over R_m^+ with ℤ_pⁿ replaced by (p^mℤ_p)ⁿ.

items.name: Local cohomology of O⁺/p as continuous group cohomology
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity, let V be an affinoid smooth adic space over Spa(K, O_K) with an étale map V → 𝕋ⁿ that factors as a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps, let 𝕃 be an 𝔽_p-local system on V_ét, and let Ṽ = V ×_{𝕋ⁿ} 𝕋̃ⁿ ∈ V_proét with \hat{Ṽ} = Spa(S, S⁺). Then Ṽ^{j/V} ≅ Ṽ × ℤ_p^{n(j−1)}, H^i(Ṽ, 𝕃 ⊗ O_V⁺/p)^a = 0 for i > 0, H^0(Ṽ, 𝕃 ⊗ O_V⁺/p)^a = M is an almost finitely generated projective S^{+a}/p-module, and H^i(V_proét, 𝕃 ⊗ O_V⁺/p)^a ≅ H^i_cont(ℤ_pⁿ, M).
items.note: Unnumbered step: Lemma 3.16 (cohomology of Ṽ × profinite set), Lemma 4.12 (almost vanishing on affinoid perfectoids) and the Cartan–Leray spectral sequence for the Galois ℤ_pⁿ-cover Ṽ → V. It gives Lemma 5.6(i) and is the local input for §5. The analogue for Â_inf in BMS1 is planned in AInfCohomology:AI.3 ('compute its continuous group cochains … and prove the almost purity comparison'), but that stage works over a smooth formal model; no stage plans this F_p-local-system statement.

items.name: Local almost vanishing above the dimension
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity. Let V be an affinoid smooth adic space over Spa(K, O_K) with an étale map V → 𝕋ⁿ that factors as a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps. Let 𝕃 be an 𝔽_p-local system on V_ét. For i > n = dim V, the cohomology group H^i(V_ét, 𝕃 ⊗ O_V⁺/p) is almost zero as an O_K-module.
items.note: From H^i(V_proét, 𝕃 ⊗ O_V⁺/p)^a ≅ H^i_cont(ℤ_pⁿ, M) and cohomological dimension n of ℤ_pⁿ. No stage plans it. Used in Lemma 5.9 for the vanishing of R^jλ_*(𝕃 ⊗ O_X⁺/p), j > dim X.

items.name: Almost finite generation of restriction images
items.statement: In the situation of Lemma 5.6 (K perfectoid of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity; V affinoid smooth over Spa(K, O_K) with an étale map V → 𝕋ⁿ factoring as a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps; 𝕃 an 𝔽_p-local system on V_ét), assume that V′ ⊂ V is a rational subset such that V′ is strictly contained in V (that is, \overline{V′} ⊂ V). Then the image of H^i(V_ét, 𝕃 ⊗ O_V⁺/p) → H^i(V′_ét, 𝕃 ⊗ O_V⁺/p) is an almost finitely generated O_K-module.
items.note: Proof (pp. 43–45): reduce to trivial 𝕃 through the Hochschild–Serre sequence of a finite Galois cover and Lemma 5.4 with N = n + 2; then pass to finite levels U_m of the perfectoid torus via Lemma 4.5, use the Hochschild–Serre sequence for p^mℤ_pⁿ ⊂ ℤ_pⁿ, Lemma 5.5, Lemma 5.4, and Lemma 5.8 (the restriction S_m^{(j)} → S_m^{(j+1)} is completely continuous; O_K is almost noetherian). This is the Cartan–Serre-type input. No stage plans it.

items.name: Images of completely continuous maps mod ϖ
items.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field, and let f: V → W be a completely continuous map of K-Banach spaces. Let V_0 ⊂ V, W_0 ⊂ W be open and bounded subsets, such that f(V_0) ⊂ W_0. Let ϖ ∈ K be some topologically nilpotent element. Then the image A of V_0/ϖ in W_0/ϖ is a subquotient of an open and bounded subset in a finite-dimensional K-vector space.
items.note: Proof: write f = f_0 + ϖf_1 with f_0 of finite-dimensional image X and f_1(V_0) ⊂ W_0; the image lies in the image of X ∩ W_0. 'Completely continuous' means a limit of finite-rank operators, as in Kiehl's finiteness theorem; Mathlib's IsCompactOperator (Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Operator/Compact/Basic.lean:71) is a different notion and this lemma is absent. Used in Lemma 5.6(ii).

items.name: Almost finiteness of cohomology of O⁺/p
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity. Let X be a proper smooth adic space over Spa(K, O_K), and let 𝕃 be an 𝔽_p-local system on X_ét. Then H^j(X_ét, 𝕃 ⊗ O_X⁺/p) is an almost finitely generated O_K-module.
items.note: The paper's 'crucial statement'. Proof (pp. 45–46): Čech spectral sequences E_1^{m_1,m_2} = ⊕_{|J|=m_1+1} H^{m_2}(V^{(k)}_{J,ét}, 𝕃 ⊗ O_X⁺/p) ⇒ H^{m_1+m_2}(X_ét, 𝕃 ⊗ O_X⁺/p) for the N = j + 2 nested covers of Lemma 5.3, then Lemma 5.4 with Lemma 5.6(ii). This is the Cartan–Serre (Kiehl) argument, cf. Kiehl [12]. No stage plans it.

items.name: Almost vanishing of cohomology of O⁺/p above 2 dim X
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity. Let X be a proper smooth adic space over Spa(K, O_K), and let 𝕃 be an 𝔽_p-local system on X_ét. Then H^j(X_ét, 𝕃 ⊗ O_X⁺/p) is almost zero for j > 2 dim X.
items.note: Proof: by Lemma 5.6(i), R^jλ_*(𝕃 ⊗ O_X⁺/p) is almost zero for j > dim X, where λ: X_ét → X_an is the projection to the site of open subsets; X_an has cohomological dimension ⩽ dim X by de Jong–van der Put [11, Proposition 2.5.8]. No stage plans it.

items.name: Tilted integral structure sheaf
items.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian adic space over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p). The tilted integral structure sheaf is Ô^+_{X♭} = lim_{←Φ} O_X⁺/p on X_proét, where the inverse limit is taken along the Frobenius map. If X lives over Spa(K, K⁺), where K is a perfectoid field with an open and bounded valuation subring K⁺ ⊂ K, we set Ô_{X♭} = Ô^+_{X♭} ⊗_{K♭+} K♭.
items.note: AInfCohomology:AI.3: 'On the analytic generic fiber X of a smooth p-adic formal scheme 𝔛, construct the completed integral structure sheaf, its tilt and the Witt A_inf,X sheaf.' The stage's scope is narrower than the paper's (any locally noetherian adic space over ℚ_p); PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational imports this A_inf sheaf 'on the analytic pro-étale site supplied by AdicEtaleGeometry'. At ring level, lim_Φ A/p is Mathlib's PreTilt (Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfection.lean:634, PreTilt O p := Perfection (ModP O p) p), but there is no sheaf version. Used in the proof of Theorem 5.1 and in Definition 6.1.

items.name: Sections of the tilted structure sheaf on affinoid perfectoids
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 with an open and bounded valuation subring K⁺ ⊂ K, let X be a locally noetherian adic space over Spa(K, K⁺), and let U ∈ X_proét be affinoid perfectoid, with \hat{U} = Spa(R, R⁺), where (R, R⁺) is a perfectoid affinoid (K, K⁺)-algebra. Let (R♭, R♭⁺) be its tilt. Then Ô^+_{X♭}(U) = R♭⁺ and Ô_{X♭}(U) = R♭.
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory's P7 packet (research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json) requests this from AInfCohomology:AI.3 for every locally noetherian adic space over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p), and AI.3's stage text owns the completed integral structure sheaf, its tilt, the Witt sheaf A_inf,X and the toric continuous-cochain computation; routed there (route 5). Proof: 'follows from Lemma 4.10 by repeating part of its proof in the tilted situation'. Used for the R lim_← computation in the proof of Theorem 5.1 and in Theorem 6.5.

items.name: Almost acyclicity of the tilted structure sheaf
items.statement: In the situation of Lemma 5.11 (K perfectoid of characteristic 0, K⁺ ⊂ K open bounded valuation subring, X locally noetherian over Spa(K, K⁺), U ∈ X_proét affinoid perfectoid with \hat{U} = Spa(R, R⁺)), the cohomology groups H^i(U, Ô^+_{X♭}) are almost zero for i > 0, with respect to the almost setting defined by K♭⁺ and its ideal of topologically nilpotent elements.
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory's P7 packet (research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json) requests this from AInfCohomology:AI.3 for every locally noetherian adic space over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p), and AI.3's stage text owns the completed integral structure sheaf, its tilt, the Witt sheaf A_inf,X and the toric continuous-cochain computation; routed there (route 5). Tilted analogue of Lemma 4.10.

items.name: Changing K⁺ to O_K does not change O⁺/p-cohomology
items.statement: Let K be an algebraically closed complete extension of ℚ_p with an open and bounded valuation subring K⁺ ⊂ K, let X be a proper smooth adic space over Spa(K, K⁺), let 𝕃 be an 𝔽_p-local system on X_ét, and let X′ = X ×_{Spa(K,K⁺)} Spa(K, O_K), an open subset of X. Then H^i(X_ét, 𝕃 ⊗ O_X⁺/p) → H^i(X′_ét, 𝕃 ⊗ O_X⁺/p) is an almost isomorphism of K⁺-modules.
items.note: Unnumbered step. Proof: compare a simplicial cover of X by affinoid perfectoids U_k with its restriction to X′ and apply Lemma 4.12 termwise. No stage plans it.

items.name: Cohomology of the tilted sheaf is free
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 5.1 (K algebraically closed, X proper smooth over Spa(K, K⁺), 𝕃 an 𝔽_p-local system), fix π ∈ O_{K♭} with π♯ = p. Then there is an integer r ⩾ 0 such that H^i(X_proét, 𝕃 ⊗ Ô^+_{X♭}/π^k)^a ≅ (O^a_{K♭}/π^k)^r for all k, compatibly with Frobenius; H^i(X_proét, 𝕃 ⊗ Ô^+_{X♭})^a ≅ (O^a_{K♭})^r; and H^i(X_proét, 𝕃 ⊗ Ô_{X♭}) ≅ (K♭)^r, compatibly with Frobenius φ.
items.note: Unnumbered steps. Uses Lemma 5.9 (Ô^+_{X♭}/π = O_X⁺/p), Lemma 2.12 (structure of almost finitely generated Frobenius modules over O_{K♭}), Corollary 4.7, Lemma 3.18 and Lemma 5.11 for R lim_←(𝕃 ⊗ Ô^+_{X♭}/π^k)^a = (𝕃 ⊗ Ô^+_{X♭})^a. No stage plans it.

items.name: Artin–Schreier sequence on the pro-étale site
items.statement: Let X be as in Theorem 5.1 and 𝕃 an 𝔽_p-local system on X_ét. The sequence 0 → 𝕃 → 𝕃 ⊗ Ô_{X♭} → 𝕃 ⊗ Ô_{X♭} → 0, where the second map is v ⊗ f ↦ v ⊗ (f^p − f), is an exact sequence of sheaves on X_proét. Consequently H^i(X_ét, 𝕃) = H^i(X_proét, 𝕃) = H^i(X_proét, 𝕃 ⊗ Ô_{X♭})^{φ=1} ≅ 𝔽_p^r.
items.note: Unnumbered step. Surjectivity is checked on affinoid perfectoid U over which 𝕃 is trivial, using \hat{U}♭_fét ≅ \hat{U}_fét and [17, Lemma 7.5(i)] (finite étale covers of \hat{U} come from X_proét); the φ-invariants use that x ↦ x^p − x is surjective on the algebraically closed K♭, and Corollary 3.17(i). PerfectoidSpaces:P3 plans the tilting equivalence of finite étale sites, which is an input; no stage plans the sequence itself.

items.name: Relative primitive comparison
items.statement: Let f: X → Y be a proper smooth morphism of locally noetherian adic spaces over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p). Let 𝕃 be an 𝔽_p-local system on X_ét. Then for all i ⩾ 0, there is an isomorphism of sheaves of almost O_Y⁺-modules (R^i f_{ét∗}𝕃) ⊗ O_Y^{+a}/p ≅ R^i f_{ét∗}(𝕃 ⊗ O_X^{+a}/p). Here, the almost setting is relative to the site Y_ét, the sheaf of algebras O_Y⁺, and the ideal of elements of valuation < 1 everywhere; if Y lives over Spa(K, K⁺) for some nondiscretely valued extension K of ℚ_p, this is the same as the almost setting with respect to K⁺ and the ideal of topologically nilpotent elements in K⁺.
items.note: No atlas stage plans the primitive comparison theorem or the finiteness of F_p-étale cohomology of proper smooth adic spaces over C; the PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-18 extraction (item 085) records the same absence. ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H0–H3 plan classical étale cohomology (ℓ-adic, curves), not this theorem. Searched atlas roadmaps for 'primitive comparison', 'finiteness', 'proper smooth adic space'; Mathlib and Tau Ceti have no étale cohomology of adic spaces (Tau Ceti AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace covers only Spa, valuation spectra and Huber rings). Proof: check at geometric points Spa(L, L⁺) → Y using Huber's proper base change [9, Proposition 2.6.1] and Theorem 5.1 for the fibre X_y.

items.name: The sheaves 𝔸_inf and 𝔹_inf
items.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian adic space over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p). On X_proét consider the sheaf 𝔸_inf = W(Ô^+_{X♭}) and its rational version 𝔹_inf = 𝔸_inf[1/p]. We have θ: 𝔸_inf → Ô_X⁺ extending to θ: 𝔹_inf → Ô_X.
items.note: AInfCohomology:AI.3: 'construct the completed integral structure sheaf, its tilt and the Witt A_inf,X sheaf' (on the generic fibre of a smooth formal scheme); PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational: 'On the analytic pro-étale site supplied by AdicEtaleGeometry import the integral A_inf sheaf from AI.3. Construct the rational structural B_dR and crystalline/semistable period sheaves'. Ring-level θ is Mathlib's WittVector.fontaineTheta (see the ring-level item).

items.name: The positive de Rham sheaf 𝔹⁺_dR
items.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian adic space over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p). The positive de Rham sheaf on X_proét is 𝔹⁺_dR = lim_← 𝔹_inf/(ker θ)^n, with its filtration Fil^i 𝔹⁺_dR = (ker θ)^i 𝔹⁺_dR.
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational: 'Construct the rational structural B_dR and crystalline/semistable period sheaves from the same rings as R06.1.' Ring-level analogue is Mathlib's BDeRhamPlus (separate item).

items.name: The de Rham sheaf 𝔹_dR
items.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian adic space over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p). The de Rham sheaf on X_proét is 𝔹_dR = 𝔹⁺_dR[t^{−1}], where t is any element that generates Fil¹𝔹⁺_dR. It has the filtration Fil^i 𝔹_dR = Σ_{j∈ℤ} t^{−j} Fil^{i+j} 𝔹⁺_dR. (Remark 6.2: locally on X_proét the element t exists, is unique up to a unit, and is not a zero-divisor, so 𝔹_dR and its filtration are well defined.)
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational: 'Construct the rational structural B_dR and crystalline/semistable period sheaves'. Well-definedness rests on Theorem 6.5(i) and Proposition 6.7.

items.name: A_inf(R, R⁺) and θ
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 with open and bounded valuation subring K⁺ ⊂ K and (R, R⁺) a perfectoid affinoid (K, K⁺)-algebra. Fix π ∈ K♭ such that π♯/p ∈ (K⁺)^×. Define 𝔸_inf(R, R⁺) = W(R♭⁺), with θ: 𝔸_inf(R, R⁺) = W(R♭⁺) → R⁺.
items.note: Mathlib: WittVector (Mathlib/RingTheory/WittVector/Defs.lean:52), PreTilt (Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfection.lean:634; PreTilt O p := Perfection (ModP O p) p = lim_Φ O/p, which is R♭⁺ for O = R⁺) and WittVector.fontaineTheta (Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FontaineTheta.lean:165, 'def fontaineTheta : 𝕎 R♭ →+* R', for R p-adically complete with p not a unit). So 𝔸_inf(R, R⁺) = WittVector p (PreTilt R⁺ p) with θ = WittVector.fontaineTheta R⁺ p. Mathlib has no perfectoid pairs; the definitions apply to R⁺, which is p-adically complete.

items.name: Surjectivity of θ
items.statement: For a perfectoid affinoid (K, K⁺)-algebra (R, R⁺) as above, θ: 𝔸_inf(R, R⁺) = W(R♭⁺) → R⁺ is surjective.
items.note: PerfectoidSpaces:P1: 'Construct Fontaine's θ, its surjectivity, and the principal non-zero-divisor description of its kernel.' Mathlib has the conditional statement surjective_fontaineTheta (Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FontaineTheta.lean:195): θ is surjective if Frobenius on R/p is surjective. Frobenius-surjectivity of R⁺/p for perfectoid (R, R⁺) is not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti, so the paper's statement is not yet library.

items.name: B_inf(R, R⁺) and B⁺_dR(R, R⁺)
items.statement: For a perfectoid affinoid (K, K⁺)-algebra (R, R⁺) as above, 𝔹_inf(R, R⁺) = 𝔸_inf(R, R⁺)[p^{−1}] and 𝔹⁺_dR(R, R⁺) = lim_← 𝔹_inf(R, R⁺)/(ker θ)^i.
items.note: Mathlib: BDeRhamPlus (Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/BDeRham.lean:77) is AdicCompletion (RingHom.ker (fontaineThetaInvertP R p)) (Localization.Away (p : 𝕎 R♭)), with fontaineThetaInvertP (line 64) the map θ[1/p]; its docstring says it is 'a generalized version of these period rings following Scholze' and cites this paper. Applied to R⁺ this is the ker θ-adic completion of W(R♭⁺)[1/p], i.e. 𝔹⁺_dR(R, R⁺).

items.name: Generator ξ of ker θ over K
items.statement: There is an element ξ ∈ 𝔸_inf(K, K⁺) that generates ker θ, where θ: 𝔸_inf(K, K⁺) → K⁺. The element ξ is not a zero-divisor, and hence is unique up to a unit.
items.note: PerfectoidSpaces:P1: 'Construct Fontaine's θ, its surjectivity, and the principal non-zero-divisor description of its kernel.' Also AInfCohomology:AI.0 ('identify the kernel generator'). Mathlib's BDeRham.lean lists 'Show that ker θ is principal when the base ring is integral perfectoid' as TODO. Proof: ξ = [π] − Σ_{i⩾1} p^i[x_i] with x_i ∈ O_{K♭}.

items.name: ξ generates ker θ for perfectoid algebras
items.statement: For any perfectoid affinoid (K, K⁺)-algebra (R, R⁺), the element ξ of Lemma 6.3 generates ker(θ: 𝔸_inf(R, R⁺) → R⁺), and is not a zero-divisor in 𝔸_inf(R, R⁺).
items.note: PerfectoidSpaces:P1: 'the principal non-zero-divisor description of its kernel' (for perfectoid Tate rings). Proof: reduce ξy = 0 modulo p using flatness of R♭⁺ over K♭⁺; divisibility by successive approximation using W(R♭⁺)/(ξ, p) = R♭⁺/π = R⁺/p and p-adic completeness.

items.name: B_dR(R, R⁺)
items.statement: For a perfectoid affinoid (K, K⁺)-algebra (R, R⁺), 𝔹_dR(R, R⁺) = 𝔹⁺_dR(R, R⁺)[ξ^{−1}].
items.note: Mathlib: BDeRham (Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/BDeRham.lean:90) localizes BDeRhamPlus at the images of all generators a of ker θ[1/p]; its docstring: 'Mathematically, this is equivalent to inverting a generator of the ideal ker θ after we show that it is principal.' The identification with 𝔹⁺_dR[ξ^{−1}] therefore uses Lemma 6.3, which is not in Mathlib.

items.name: Filtration on B_dR(R, R⁺)
items.statement: For a perfectoid affinoid (K, K⁺)-algebra (R, R⁺), Fil^i 𝔹_dR(R, R⁺) = ξ^i 𝔹⁺_dR(R, R⁺), i ∈ ℤ.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/bdr-plus-of-perfectoid-affinoid-algebras (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Mathlib defines BDeRham but no filtration. PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1 plans 'B_dR^+, its filtration and B_dR' only for C_p ('Import C_p and its tilt'), not for perfectoid algebras.

items.name: Graded pieces of B_dR(R, R⁺)
items.statement: For any i ∈ ℤ, we have gr^i 𝔹_dR(R, R⁺) ≅ ξ^i R, which is a free R-module of rank one. In particular, gr^•𝔹_dR(R, R⁺) ≅ R[ξ^{±1}].
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/bdr-plus-of-perfectoid-affinoid-algebras (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Proof: ξ generates ker θ in 𝔹_inf and is not a zero-divisor. R06.1 plans filtration properties of B_dR only for C_p; not in Mathlib.

items.name: Period sheaves on affinoid perfectoids
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 with open and bounded valuation subring K⁺, and let X be a locally noetherian adic space over Spa(K, K⁺). Assume that U ∈ X_proét is affinoid perfectoid, with \hat{U} = Spa(R, R⁺). Then we have a canonical isomorphism 𝔸_inf(U) = 𝔸_inf(R, R⁺), and analogous statements for 𝔹_inf, 𝔹⁺_dR and 𝔹_dR. In particular, there is an element ξ generating Fil¹𝔹⁺_dR(U), unique up to a unit, and it is not a zero-divisor.
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory's P7 packet (research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json) requests this from AInfCohomology:AI.3 for every locally noetherian adic space over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p), and AI.3's stage text owns the completed integral structure sheaf, its tilt, the Witt sheaf A_inf,X and the toric continuous-cochain computation; routed there (route 5). Proof: induction on m for W(Ô^+_{X♭})/p^m, Lemma 3.18, a direct limit for 𝔹_inf, and exactness of 0 → 𝔹_inf →^{ξ^i} 𝔹_inf → 𝔹_inf/(ker θ)^i → 0 on sections over U. The almost setting is that of 𝔸_inf(K, K⁺) and the ideal generated by all [π^{1/p^N}]. Its rational part (𝔹_inf, 𝔹⁺_dR, 𝔹_dR and ξ) is PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/period-sheaves-on-affinoid-perfectoids; the integral statement 𝔸_inf(U) = W(R♭⁺) is the request.

items.name: Almost acyclicity of period sheaves
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 6.5 (U ∈ X_proét affinoid perfectoid over Spa(K, K⁺)), all H^i(U, F) are almost zero for i > 0, where F is any of the sheaves 𝔸_inf, 𝔹_inf, 𝔹⁺_dR, 𝔹_dR; the almost setting is with respect to 𝔸_inf(K, K⁺) and the ideal generated by all [π^{1/p^N}].
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational: 'Prove rational local acyclicity, filtration strictness and the relative Poincaré lemma'; the integral statement is in the scope of AInfCohomology:AI.3.

items.name: Acyclicity of 𝔹⁺_dR and 𝔹_dR
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 6.5, in 𝔹⁺_dR(U) and 𝔹_dR(U) the element [π] becomes invertible; in particular the cohomology groups H^i(U, F) vanish for i > 0 for these sheaves.
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational: 'Prove rational local acyclicity'. Proof: [π] maps to the unit π♯ ∈ K^× in 𝔹_inf/(ker θ).

items.name: Sections over U × S
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 with open and bounded valuation subring K⁺, let X be a locally noetherian adic space over Spa(K, K⁺), and assume that U ∈ X_proét is affinoid perfectoid. Further, let S be some profinite set, and V = U × S ∈ X_proét, which is again affinoid perfectoid. Then F(V) = Hom_cont(S, F(U)) for any of the sheaves F ∈ {Ô_X, Ô_X⁺, Ô_{X♭}, Ô^+_{X♭}, 𝔸_inf, 𝔹_inf, 𝔹⁺_dR, 𝔹_dR, gr^i𝔹_dR}. Here, Ô_X⁺(U) is given the p-adic topology, and all other period sheaves are given the induced topology: 𝔸_inf(U) the inverse limit topology, 𝔹_inf(U) the direct limit topology, the quotients (𝔹_inf/(ker θ)^n)(U) the quotient topology, and then 𝔹⁺_dR(U) the inverse limit topology and 𝔹_dR(U) the direct limit topology.
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory's P7 packet (research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json) requests this from AInfCohomology:AI.3 for every locally noetherian adic space over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p), and AI.3's stage text owns the completed integral structure sheaf, its tilt, the Witt sheaf A_inf,X and the toric continuous-cochain computation; routed there (route 5). Proof: 'Go through all identifications.' Source of continuous group cohomology in Proposition 6.16 and §§7–8. Its rational cases are PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/period-sheaves-on-profinite-products; the cases Ô_X⁺, Ô_{X♭}, Ô⁺_{X♭} and 𝔸_inf are the request.

items.name: Tate twist of pro-étale sheaves
items.statement: Let \hat{ℤ}_p = lim_← ℤ/pⁿℤ as sheaves on X_proét, and \hat{ℤ}_p(1) = lim_← μ_{pⁿ}, which is locally free of rank one over \hat{ℤ}_p. For any sheaf F of \hat{ℤ}_p-modules on X_proét and i ∈ ℤ, set F(i) = F ⊗_{\hat{ℤ}_p} \hat{ℤ}_p(1)^{⊗i}.
items.note: Planned: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tate-twists (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H0 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H0.json, merged before this extraction. Notation used in Proposition 6.7 and Corollaries 6.14 and 6.19.

items.name: Graded pieces of 𝔹_dR are Tate twists of Ô_X
items.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian adic space over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p). For all i ∈ ℤ, we have gr^i 𝔹_dR ≅ Ô_X(i).
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/graded-de-rham-period-sheaf-tate-twist (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Proof: over the completion K of ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}), t = log([ε]) ∈ Fil¹𝔹⁺_dR(K, K⁺) generates Fil¹, so gr^i𝔹_dR = t^iÔ_X on X_{K,proét} ≅ X_proét/X_K (Proposition 3.15); descend using that Gal(ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞})/ℚ_p) acts on t through the cyclotomic character.

items.name: Pro-étale sheaf of differentials
items.statement: Let X be a smooth adic space over Spa(k, O_k), where k is a discretely valued complete nonarchimedean extension of ℚ_p with perfect residue field κ. On X_proét, Ω_X^1 = ν^*Ω^1_{X_ét}, and its exterior powers Ω_X^i.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/corrected-structural-de-rham-sheaf (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. ν: X_proét → X_ét is the projection. Ingredient of the connection in Remark 6.9.

items.name: The sheaf 𝒪𝔹_inf
items.statement: Let X be a smooth adic space over Spa(k, O_k), k a discretely valued complete nonarchimedean extension of ℚ_p with perfect residue field κ. On X_proét, 𝒪𝔹_inf = O_X ⊗_{W(κ)} 𝔹_inf, where W(κ) = ν^*W(κ) is the constant sheaf associated with W(κ). It admits a map θ: 𝒪𝔹_inf → Ô_X.
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational: 'Construct the rational structural B_dR … period sheaves'. PadicHodgeTheory:P8 ('Corrected structural period-sheaf construction') warns that the uncompleted tensor formula is not used for 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR; the 2016 corrigendum replaces the use of 𝒪𝔹_inf by a p-adically completed tensor product (see Definition 6.8(iii)).

items.name: The positive structural de Rham sheaf 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR (corrected)
items.statement: Let X be a smooth adic space over Spa(k, O_k), k a discretely valued complete nonarchimedean extension of ℚ_p with perfect residue field κ. Fix any affinoid perfectoid U = lim_← U_i in X_proét, U_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺), with perfectoid affinoid completed direct limit (R, R⁺) of the (R_i, R_i⁺). Then 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR is the sheafification of the presheaf sending U to the direct limit over i of the ker θ-adic completion of (R_i⁺ ⊗̂_{W(κ)} 𝔸_inf(R, R⁺))[1/p]. Here the completed tensor product is the p-adic completion of the tensor product, and θ: (R_i⁺ ⊗̂_{W(κ)} 𝔸_inf(R, R⁺))[1/p] → R is the tensor product of the map R_i⁺ → R⁺ and the usual map θ: 𝔸_inf(R, R⁺) → R⁺. Its filtration is Fil^i𝒪𝔹⁺_dR = (ker θ)^i 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR.
items.locator: §6, Definition 6.8(iii), p. 51 (as corrected in Forum Math. Pi 4 (2016) e6, item (3))
items.note: CORRECTED per the 2016 corrigendum: the printed definition 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR = lim_← 𝒪𝔹_inf/(ker θ)^n is wrong; 'as in Brinon's book, one has to take a suitable p-adic completion of 𝒪𝔹_inf = O_X ⊗_{W(κ)} 𝔹_inf first'. PadicHodgeTheory:P8 ('Corrected structural period-sheaf construction'): 'Apply Scholze's 2013 corrigendum throughout P8: the structural B_dR^+ sheaf is formed using the p-adically completed tensor with A_inf before p-inversion and kernel-of-theta completion, followed by the specified colimit/sheafification. The uncompleted tensor formula is not used.' P8:local-rational: 'Construct the rational structural B_dR … period sheaves'.

items.name: The structural de Rham sheaf 𝒪𝔹_dR
items.statement: In the situation of Definition 6.8, the structural de Rham sheaf is 𝒪𝔹_dR = 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR[t^{−1}], where t is a generator of Fil¹𝔹⁺_dR, with the filtration Fil^i𝒪𝔹_dR = Σ_{j∈ℤ} t^{−j} Fil^{i+j}𝒪𝔹⁺_dR. (Remark 6.9: because locally on X_proét the element t exists, is unique up to a unit and is not a zero-divisor, 𝒪𝔹_dR and its filtrations are well defined.)
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational: 'Construct the rational structural B_dR and crystalline/semistable period sheaves'. Uses the corrected 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR.

items.name: Connection on 𝒪𝔹_dR
items.statement: The sheaf 𝒪𝔹_inf admits a unique 𝔹_inf-linear connection ∇: 𝒪𝔹_inf → 𝒪𝔹_inf ⊗_{O_X} Ω_X^1 extending the one on O_X. This connection extends uniquely to the completion ∇: 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR → 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR ⊗_{O_X} Ω_X^1, and this extension is 𝔹⁺_dR-linear. Because t ∈ 𝔹⁺_dR, it further extends to a 𝔹_dR-linear connection ∇: 𝒪𝔹_dR → 𝒪𝔹_dR ⊗_{O_X} Ω_X^1.
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational plans 'the relative Poincaré lemma', which is the exactness of the de Rham complex of this connection. With the corrected definition the connection must be extended through the p-adically completed tensor product R_i⁺ ⊗̂_{W(κ)} 𝔸_inf(R, R⁺) before the ker θ-adic completion.

items.name: Elements u_i and the tower X̃
items.statement: Choose an algebraic extension of k whose completion K is perfectoid; let X_K be the base change of X to Spa(K, O_K). Assume given an étale map X → 𝕋ⁿ (such a map exists locally on X), let X̃ = X ×_{𝕋ⁿ} 𝕋̃ⁿ; then X̃_K ∈ X_{K,proét} ≅ X_proét/X_K is perfectoid. On X_proét/X̃ put u_i = T_i ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ [T_i♭] ∈ 𝒪𝔹_inf|_{X̃} = (O_X ⊗_{W(κ)} W(Ô^+_{X♭}))|_{X̃}, which lie in ker θ, where T_i♭ ∈ Ô^+_{X♭} = lim_← O_X⁺/p is given by the sequence (T_i, T_i^{1/p}, …).
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/local-structure-of-structural-de-rham-sheaf (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Setup for Proposition 6.10. With the corrected definition the u_i are the images in 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR.

items.name: Local structure of 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR
items.statement: In the situation above (X smooth over Spa(k, O_k) with an étale map X → 𝕋ⁿ, X̃ = X ×_{𝕋ⁿ} 𝕋̃ⁿ), the map 𝔹⁺_dR|_{X̃}[[X_1, …, X_n]] → 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR|_{X̃} sending X_i to u_i is an isomorphism of sheaves over X_proét/X̃, where 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR is the corrected sheaf of Definition 6.8(iii).
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/local-structure-of-structural-de-rham-sheaf (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Holds only with the corrected definition of 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR (2016 corrigendum, item (3)); with the printed definition the composite 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR → 𝔹⁺_dR[[X]] → 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR need not be the identity. Proof: 𝔹⁺_dR|_{X̃_K}[[X_1, …, X_n]] carries a unique O_X|_{X̃_K}-algebra structure sending T_i to [T_i♭] + X_i, compatible with 𝔹⁺_dR[[X]]/(ker θ) = Ô_X (Lemmas 6.11, 6.12 and Hensel's lemma), giving an inverse.

items.name: Strengthened Proposition 6.10 (corrigendum)
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 6.10, assume that U ∈ X_proét/X̃_K is affinoid perfectoid, U = lim_← U_i, U_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺), with perfectoid affinoid completed direct limit (R, R⁺). Then for any sufficiently large i, the ker θ-adic completion S_i of (R_i⁺ ⊗̂_{W(κ)} 𝔸_inf(R, R⁺))[1/p] is isomorphic to 𝔹⁺_dR(R, R⁺)[[X_1, …, X_n]], via the map constructed in the proof of Proposition 6.10. In particular, this is independent of i, and 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR(U) = 𝔹⁺_dR(R, R⁺)[[X_1, …, X_n]], as the right-hand side already defines a sheaf on X_proét/X̃.
items.locator: Corrigendum (Forum Math. Pi 4 (2016) e6), strengthening §6, Proposition 6.10, p. 52
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/local-structure-of-structural-de-rham-sheaf (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Added by the 2016 corrigendum. Proof there: the composite 𝔹⁺_dR(R,R⁺)[[X]] → S_i → 𝔹⁺_dR(R,R⁺)[[X]] is the identity; for S_i → 𝔹⁺_dR(R,R⁺)[[X]] → S_i it suffices that (𝔹⁺_dR(R,R⁺)/ξ^r)[X_1,…,X_n]/(X_1,…,X_n)^r → (R_i⁺ ⊗̂_{W(κ)} 𝔸_inf(R,R⁺))[1/p]/(ker θ)^r is surjective for each r ⩾ 1, using that R_i⁺[X]/(X)^r → (R_i⁺ ⊗̂_{W(κ)} R_i⁺)/(ker θ_i)^r is injective with cokernel killed by a power of p.

items.name: Maps into 𝔹⁺_dR[[X]] extend to p-adic completions
items.statement: Let (R, R⁺) be a perfectoid affinoid (K, O_K)-algebra, so we get 𝔹⁺_dR(R, R⁺). Let S be a finitely generated O_k-algebra. Then any morphism f: S → 𝔹⁺_dR(R, R⁺)[[X_1, …, X_n]] such that θ(f(S)) ⊂ R⁺ extends to the p-adic completion of S.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/bdr-plus-power-series-extension-lemma (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Proof: modulo (ker θ)^i the image of S lies in (W(R♭⁺)[[X_1, …, X_n]]/(ker θ)^i)[ξ/p^k, X_1/p^k, …, X_n/p^k] for some k, which is p-adically complete. Used in the proof of Proposition 6.10.

items.name: Algebraic models of étale maps to the torus
items.statement: Let U = Spa(R, R⁺) over Spa(W(κ)[p^{−1}], W(κ)) be an affinoid adic space of finite type with an étale map U → 𝕋ⁿ. Then there exists a finitely generated W(κ)[T_1^{±1}, …, T_n^{±1}]-algebra R_0⁺, such that R_0 = R_0⁺[1/p] is étale over W(κ)[p^{−1}][T_1^{±1}, …, T_n^{±1}] and R⁺ is the p-adic completion of R_0⁺.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/etale-algebras-over-torus-models (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Proof: Huber [9, Corollary 1.7.3(ii),(iii)] and [9, Remark 1.2.6(iii)], plus excellence of W(κ) (normalization of a reduced flat finitely generated W(κ)-algebra S⁺ in S⁺[p^{−1}] is finite).

items.name: Poincaré lemma
items.statement: Let X be an n-dimensional smooth adic space over Spa(k, O_k). The following sequence of sheaves on X_proét is exact: 0 → 𝔹⁺_dR → 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR →^∇ 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR ⊗_{O_X} Ω_X^1 →^∇ ⋯ →^∇ 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR ⊗_{O_X} Ω_X^n → 0. Moreover, the derivation ∇ satisfies Griffiths transversality with respect to the filtration on 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR, and with respect to the grading giving Ω_X^i degree i, the sequence is strict exact.
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational: 'Prove rational local acyclicity, filtration strictness and the relative Poincaré lemma.' Proof: immediate from Proposition 6.10 (with the corrected 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR). Extractions of PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-18 (item 093) and PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17 (item 130) route it to the same stage.

items.name: Faltings' extension
items.statement: Let X be a smooth adic space over Spa(k, O_k). Then we have a short exact sequence of sheaves over X_proét: 0 → Ô_X(1) → gr¹𝒪𝔹⁺_dR → Ô_X ⊗_{O_X} Ω_X^1 → 0.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/faltings-extension (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Proof: first graded piece of the Poincaré lemma. P8:local-rational plans 'filtration strictness and the relative Poincaré lemma' but does not name Faltings' extension; HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T2 plans only the Hodge–Tate sequence of abelian schemes. Used for Corollary 6.19 (R¹ν_*Ô_X(1) ≅ Ω¹).

items.name: Graded pieces of 𝒪𝔹_dR
items.statement: Let X → 𝕋ⁿ, X̃, and so on, be as above. For any i ∈ ℤ, we have an isomorphism of sheaves over X_proét/X̃_K: gr^i𝒪𝔹_dR ≅ ξ^i Ô_X[X_1/ξ, …, X_n/ξ]. In particular, gr^•𝒪𝔹_dR ≅ Ô_X[ξ^{±1}, X_1, …, X_n], where ξ and all X_i have degree one.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/graded-structural-de-rham-sheaf-local-description (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. From Proposition 6.10 and Corollary 6.4.

items.name: Cohomology of gr⁰𝒪𝔹_dR over K
items.statement: Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid adic space of finite type over Spa(k, O_k) with an étale map X → 𝕋ⁿ that factors as a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps. Assume that K contains all p-power roots of unity. Then H^q(X_K, gr⁰𝒪𝔹_dR) = 0 unless q = 0, in which case it is given by R ⊗̂_k K.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/cohomology-of-graded-structural-de-rham-sheaf-over-cyclotomic-base (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. K is the perfectoid completion of an algebraic extension of k fixed before Proposition 6.10. Proof follows Brinon [4, Proposition 4.1.2]: Cartan–Leray for the ℤ_pⁿ-cover X̃_K → X_K, gr⁰𝒪𝔹_dR(X̃_K) = R̃[V_1, …, V_n] with V_i = t^{−1}log([T_i♭]/T_i), Lemma 6.17, Lemma 6.18 and Lemma 5.5.

items.name: Cohomology of gr^i𝒪𝔹_dR over k
items.statement: Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid adic space of finite type over Spa(k, O_k) with an étale map X → 𝕋ⁿ that factors as a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps. Then H^q(X, gr^i𝒪𝔹_dR) = 0 unless i = 0 and q = 0, 1. If i = 0, we have (gr⁰𝒪𝔹_dR)(X) = R and H¹(X, gr⁰𝒪𝔹_dR) = R log χ. Here, χ: Gal(\bar{k}/k) → ℤ_p^× is the cyclotomic character and log χ ∈ Hom_cont(Gal(\bar{k}/k), ℚ_p) = H¹_cont(Gal(\bar{k}/k), ℚ_p) is its logarithm.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/cohomology-of-graded-structural-de-rham-sheaf (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Proof: H^q(X, gr^i𝒪𝔹_dR) = H^q_cont(Γ_k, R ⊗̂_k K(i)) with K the completion of k(μ_{p^∞}), Γ_k = Gal(k(μ_{p^∞})/k), then Tate's computation [18] of H^q_cont(Γ_k, ℚ_p(i)).

items.name: Action of γ_i on V_j
items.statement: In the proof of Proposition 6.16(i) (V_j = t^{−1}log([T_j♭]/T_j), t = log([ε]), γ_i ∈ ℤ_pⁿ the ith basis vector), the action of γ_i on V_j is given by γ_i(V_j) = V_j if i ≠ j and γ_i(V_i) = V_i + 1.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/gamma-action-on-log-coordinates (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. γ_i multiplies T_i♭ by ε and fixes T_j♭ for j ≠ i.

items.name: R̃⁺ as a completed base change up to bounded torsion
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 6.16 (X = Spa(R, R⁺), X̃_K with \hat{X̃}_K = Spa(R̃, R̃⁺)), the map R⁺ ⊗̂_{O_k⟨T_1^{±1},…,T_n^{±1}⟩} O_K⟨T_1^{±1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{±1/p^∞}⟩ → R̃⁺ is injective with cokernel killed by some power of p. In particular, R̃ = R ⊗̂_{k⟨T_1^{±1},…,T_n^{±1}⟩} K⟨T_1^{±1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{±1/p^∞}⟩.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/perfectoid-torus-cover-completed-tensor (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Proof: 'an immediate consequence of Lemma 4.5(ii)'. Reduces Proposition 6.16(i) to Lemma 5.5.

items.name: Pushforwards of 𝒪𝔹_dR and Ô_X to the étale site
items.statement: Let X be a smooth adic space over Spa(k, O_k). Then ν_*𝒪𝔹_dR = O_{X_ét}. Moreover, ν_*Ô_X = O_{X_ét}, ν_*Ô_X(n) = 0 for n ⩾ 1, R¹ν_*Ô_X(1) ≅ Ω¹_{X_ét} via the connecting map in Faltings' extension, and R¹ν_*Ô_X(n) = 0 for n ⩾ 2.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/pushforward-of-structural-de-rham-sheaf (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Proof (printed after Remark 6.20): from Proposition 6.16(ii) and the 0th and nth graded pieces of the Poincaré lemma after inverting t.

items.name: All higher pushforwards of Ô_X(j)
items.statement: Let X be a smooth adic space over Spa(k, O_k). The sheaves R^iν_*Ô_X(j) are 0 if i < j or i > j + 1; they are Ω^j_{X_ét} if i = j, and Ω^j_{X_ét} log χ if i = j + 1.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/higher-direct-images-of-twisted-completed-structure-sheaf (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Stated without proof. The printed text has Ω^i_{X_ét} log χ for i = j + 1; this is corrected to Ω^j_{X_ét} log χ (PAPER-SCHOLZE-13/E13): for j = 0, Proposition 6.16(ii) and the Poincaré lemma give R¹ν_*Ô_X = O_{X_ét}·log χ.

items.name: B_dR^+-local system
items.statement: Let X be a smooth adic space over Spa(k, 𝒪_k), with k a discretely valued complete nonarchimedean extension of ℚ_p with perfect residue field κ (standing hypothesis of §7). A 𝔹_dR^+-local system is a sheaf of 𝔹_dR^+-modules 𝕄 on X_proét that is locally on X_proét free of finite rank.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/bdr-plus-local-system (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Searched Mathlib/Tau Ceti for BdR/de Rham/connection/Griffiths: only Mathlib's period rings BDeRhamPlus/BDeRham (Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/BDeRham.lean:77,90), no sheaves on X_proét. 𝔹_dR^+ is the pro-étale period sheaf of §6 (Definition 6.1). Used in Theorems 7.2, 7.6, 7.11 and all of §8.

items.name: 𝒪𝔹_dR^+-module with integrable connection
items.statement: Let X be a smooth adic space over Spa(k, 𝒪_k), with k a discretely valued complete nonarchimedean extension of ℚ_p with perfect residue field κ (standing hypothesis of §7). An 𝒪𝔹_dR^+-module with integrable connection is a sheaf of 𝒪𝔹_dR^+-modules ℳ on X_proét that is locally on X_proét free of finite rank, together with an integrable connection ∇_ℳ : ℳ → ℳ ⊗_{𝒪_X} Ω_X^1, satisfying the Leibniz rule with respect to the derivation ∇ on 𝒪𝔹_dR^+.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/bdr-plus-local-system (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Searched Mathlib/Tau Ceti for BdR/de Rham/connection/Griffiths: only Mathlib's period rings BDeRhamPlus/BDeRham (Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/BDeRham.lean:77,90), no sheaves on X_proét. 𝒪𝔹_dR^+ must be taken with the corrected definition of the 2016 corrigendum (ker θ-adic completion of (R_i^+ ⊗̂_{W(κ)} A_inf(R,R^+))[1/p]); ∇ is the connection of §6.

items.name: B_dR^+-local systems ≃ 𝒪𝔹_dR^+-modules with integrable connection
items.statement: Let X be a smooth adic space over Spa(k, 𝒪_k), with k a discretely valued complete nonarchimedean extension of ℚ_p with perfect residue field κ (standing hypothesis of §7). The functor 𝕄 ↦ (ℳ, ∇_ℳ) given by ℳ = 𝕄 ⊗_{𝔹_dR^+} 𝒪𝔹_dR^+, ∇_ℳ = id ⊗ ∇ induces an equivalence of categories between the category of 𝔹_dR^+-local systems and the category of 𝒪𝔹_dR^+-modules with integrable connection. The inverse functor is given by 𝕄 = ℳ^{∇_ℳ=0}.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/bdr-plus-local-systems-and-integrable-connections (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Searched Mathlib/Tau Ceti for BdR/de Rham/connection/Griffiths: only Mathlib's period rings BDeRhamPlus/BDeRham (Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/BDeRham.lean:77,90), no sheaves on X_proét. Proof: one composition is the identity; enough horizontal sections is local, reducing to X étale over 𝕋^n, where Proposition 6.10 (in the strengthened form of the corrigendum: 𝒪𝔹_dR^+(U) = 𝔹_dR^+(R,R^+)[[X_1,…,X_n]] for affinoid perfectoid U over X̃_K) and the fact that any module with integrable connection over R[[X_1,…,X_n]], R a ℚ-algebra, has enough horizontal sections, conclude. The formal-power-series fact is not in Mathlib (no connections on modules).

items.name: Locally free modules on X_an, X_ét, X_proét agree
items.statement: Let X be a smooth adic space over Spa(k, 𝒪_k), with k a discretely valued complete nonarchimedean extension of ℚ_p with perfect residue field κ (standing hypothesis of §7). Let X_an be the site of open subsets of X. Then the following categories are naturally equivalent (via pullback along λ : X_ét → X_an and ν : X_proét → X_ét): (i) the category of 𝒪_{X_an}-modules ℰ_an over X_an that are locally on X_an free of finite rank; (ii) the category of 𝒪_{X_ét}-modules ℰ_ét over X_ét that are locally on X_ét free of finite rank; (iii) the category of 𝒪_X-modules ℰ over X_proét that are locally on X_proét free of finite rank.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/vector-bundles-on-analytic-etale-and-proetale-sites (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Proof: 𝒪_{X_an} ≅ λ_*𝒪_{X_ét}, 𝒪_{X_ét} ≅ ν_*𝒪_X give full faithfulness; essential surjectivity by faithfully flat descent along finite étale R → S (reducing by [11, Proposition 3.2.2]) and along R → R_∞ = lim R_i for a pro-finite-étale presentation U = lim U_i → U_0. Nothing in Mathlib/Tau Ceti (no vector bundles on adic spaces).

items.name: Filtered 𝒪_X-module with integrable connection
items.statement: Let X be a smooth adic space over Spa(k, 𝒪_k), with k a discretely valued complete nonarchimedean extension of ℚ_p with perfect residue field κ (standing hypothesis of §7). A filtered 𝒪_X-module with integrable connection is a locally free 𝒪_X-module ℰ on X, together with a separated and exhaustive decreasing filtration Fil^iℰ, i ∈ ℤ, by locally direct summands, and an integrable connection ∇ satisfying Griffiths transversality with respect to the filtration.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/filtered-module-with-integrable-connection (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. By Lemma 7.3 it does not matter on which site ℰ lives. Mathlib has no connections on sheaves of modules.

items.name: Associated 𝒪𝔹_dR^+-module and filtered module
items.statement: Let X be a smooth adic space over Spa(k, 𝒪_k), with k a discretely valued complete nonarchimedean extension of ℚ_p with perfect residue field κ (standing hypothesis of §7). An 𝒪𝔹_dR^+-module with integrable connection ℳ and a filtered 𝒪_X-module with integrable connection ℰ are associated if there is an isomorphism of sheaves on X_proét: ℳ ⊗_{𝒪𝔹_dR^+} 𝒪𝔹_dR ≅ ℰ ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒪𝔹_dR, compatible with filtrations and connections.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/filtered-module-with-integrable-connection (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Searched Mathlib/Tau Ceti for BdR/de Rham/connection/Griffiths: only Mathlib's period rings BDeRhamPlus/BDeRham (Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/BDeRham.lean:77,90), no sheaves on X_proét. 𝒪𝔹_dR = 𝒪𝔹_dR^+[t^{-1}] with its filtration (§6). Via Theorem 7.2 one also speaks of a 𝔹_dR^+-local system being associated with ℰ (used in Definition 8.3).

items.name: Horizontal sections recover 𝕄 from ℰ
items.statement: Let X be a smooth adic space over Spa(k, 𝒪_k), with k a discretely valued complete nonarchimedean extension of ℚ_p with perfect residue field κ (standing hypothesis of §7). If ℳ is an 𝒪𝔹_dR^+-module with integrable connection and horizontal sections 𝕄, which is associated with a filtered 𝒪_X-module with integrable connection ℰ, then 𝕄 = Fil^0(ℰ ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒪𝔹_dR)^{∇=0}.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/associated-bdr-plus-local-system (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Searched Mathlib/Tau Ceti for BdR/de Rham/connection/Griffiths: only Mathlib's period rings BDeRhamPlus/BDeRham (Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/BDeRham.lean:77,90), no sheaves on X_proét. Proof: 𝕄 = Fil^0(𝕄 ⊗_{𝔹_dR^+} 𝔹_dR) = Fil^0(ℳ ⊗_{𝒪𝔹_dR^+} 𝒪𝔹_dR)^{∇=0} = Fil^0(ℰ ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒪𝔹_dR)^{∇=0}, using the Poincaré lemma (Corollary 6.13).

items.name: ℰ recovered as ν_* of 𝕄 ⊗ 𝒪𝔹_dR
items.statement: Let X be a smooth adic space over Spa(k, 𝒪_k), with k a discretely valued complete nonarchimedean extension of ℚ_p with perfect residue field κ (standing hypothesis of §7). In the situation of Theorem 7.6(i), one can reconstruct ℰ with filtration and connection via ℰ_ét ≅ ν_*(𝕄 ⊗_{𝔹_dR^+} 𝒪𝔹_dR), where ν : X_proét → X_ét.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/associated-bdr-plus-local-system (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Searched Mathlib/Tau Ceti for BdR/de Rham/connection/Griffiths: only Mathlib's period rings BDeRhamPlus/BDeRham (Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/BDeRham.lean:77,90), no sheaves on X_proét. Proof: Corollary 6.19 (ν_*𝒪𝔹_dR = 𝒪_{X_ét}) gives ℰ_ét = ν_*(ℰ ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒪𝔹_dR) = ν_*(ℳ ⊗ 𝒪𝔹_dR) = ν_*(𝕄 ⊗_{𝔹_dR^+} 𝒪𝔹_dR).

items.name: Every filtered module with connection has an associated B_dR^+-local system
items.statement: Let X be a smooth adic space over Spa(k, 𝒪_k), with k a discretely valued complete nonarchimedean extension of ℚ_p with perfect residue field κ (standing hypothesis of §7). For any filtered 𝒪_X-module with integrable connection ℰ, the sheaf 𝕄 = Fil^0(ℰ ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒪𝔹_dR)^{∇=0} is a 𝔹_dR^+-local system such that ℰ is associated with ℳ = 𝕄 ⊗_{𝔹_dR^+} 𝒪𝔹_dR^+.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/associated-bdr-plus-local-system (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Searched Mathlib/Tau Ceti for BdR/de Rham/connection/Griffiths: only Mathlib's period rings BDeRhamPlus/BDeRham (Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/BDeRham.lean:77,90), no sheaves on X_proét. Proof by induction on m − n (n maximal with Fil^nℰ = ℰ, m minimal with Fil^{m+1}ℰ = 0): the case n = m is 𝕄 = 𝕄_0 ⊗_{𝔹_dR^+} Fil^{−n}𝔹_dR; the inductive step uses the diagram of p. 61 and Lemma 7.7, concluding from the isomorphism 𝕄 ⊗_{𝔹_dR^+} Fil^0𝒪𝔹_dR ≅ Fil^0(ℰ ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒪𝔹_dR) (flatness of Fil^0𝒪𝔹_dR over 𝔹_dR^+).

items.name: Fully faithful functor from filtered modules with connection to B_dR^+-local systems
items.statement: Let X be a smooth adic space over Spa(k, 𝒪_k), with k a discretely valued complete nonarchimedean extension of ℚ_p with perfect residue field κ (standing hypothesis of §7). items.name: de Rham complex DR(ℰ), its filtration, and Hodge cohomology
items.statement: Let X be a proper smooth adic space over Spa(k, 𝒪_k) and (ℰ, ∇, Fil^•) a filtered module with integrable connection. The de Rham complex is DR(ℰ) = (0 → ℰ →^∇ ℰ ⊗ Ω_X^1 →^∇ ⋯), filtered by the subcomplexes Fil^m DR(ℰ) = (0 → Fil^mℰ →^∇ Fil^{m−1}ℰ ⊗ Ω_X^1 →^∇ ⋯).
