items.name: Graded comparison RΓ(A) ⊗ gr^iB_dR ≃ RΓ(A ⊗ gr^i𝒪𝔹_dR)
items.statement: Let X be a proper smooth adic space over Spa(k, 𝒪_k) (k as in Theorem 7.11) and 𝒜 a locally free 𝒪_X-module of finite rank. Then for all i ∈ ℤ, the map RΓ(X_k̄, 𝒜) ⊗_k̄ gr^iB_dR → RΓ(X_k̄, 𝒜 ⊗_{𝒪_X} gr^i𝒪𝔹_dR) is a quasi-isomorphism.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/coherent-cohomology-against-graded-structural-sheaf (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Proof: twist to i = 0, where gr^0B_dR = k̄̂ and the claim is H^i(X_k̄, 𝒜) ⊗_k̄ k̄̂ ≅ H^i(X_k̄, 𝒜 ⊗ gr^0𝒪𝔹_dR); LHS = H^i(X_an, 𝒜) ⊗_k k̄̂ (Proposition 9.2, Lemma 3.16), RHS = H^i(X_{k̄̂,an}, 𝒜_{k̄̂}) (Proposition 6.16(i)); conclude by finiteness and base-field compatibility of coherent cohomology.

items.name: Finiteness of coherent cohomology of proper adic spaces (Kiehl)
items.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field, f : X → S a proper morphism of adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(K, 𝒪_K), and ℱ a coherent 𝒪_X-module. Then R^if_*ℱ is coherent; in particular for S = Spa(K, 𝒪_K) the groups H^i(X, ℱ) are finite-dimensional over K, and they are computed by a Čech complex whose boundary maps have closed image.
items.locator: §7, proof of Lemma 7.13, p. 66; §8, Lemma 8.7(iii), pp. 70–71 (citing [12])
items.note: AdicSpacesPartII:R3: 'Establish Kiehl-type proper finiteness/coherence and the analytic comparison statements actually used for compactifications.' Cited input: [12] Kiehl, Der Endlichkeitssatz für eigentliche Abbildungen.

items.name: Coherent cohomology commutes with extension of the base field
items.statement: Let X be a proper adic space over Spa(k, 𝒪_k) and 𝒜 a coherent (e.g. locally free) 𝒪_X-module. For a complete extension K/k, H^i(X_K, 𝒜_K) ≅ H^i(X, 𝒜) ⊗_k K.
items.note: Planned: AdicSpacesPartII:R3/proper-coherent-cohomology-field-extension (AdicSpacesPartII packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/AdicSpacesPartII.json, merged before this extraction. Used with K = k̄̂ in Lemma 7.13. Not named by any stage (AdicSpacesPartII:R3 plans finiteness/coherence and sheaf base change, not cohomology base change along a field extension).

items.name: Fontaine's period rings B_dR^+ and B_dR
items.statement: For K = k̄̂ (or any perfectoid ring R), B_dR^+ = 𝔹_dR^+(K, 𝒪_K) is the (ker θ)-adic completion of W(𝒪_K^♭)[1/p], where θ : W(𝒪_K^♭)[1/p] → K is Fontaine's map, and B_dR = B_dR^+[ξ^{−1}] for a generator ξ of ker θ; B_dR is Fontaine's field of p-adic periods, with filtration Fil^iB_dR = ξ^iB_dR^+ and gr^0B_dR = K.
items.note: Read Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/BDeRham.lean:77 (BDeRhamPlus: AdicCompletion of Localization.Away p (𝕎 R♭) at ker fontaineThetaInvertP) and :90 (BDeRham: localization of BDeRhamPlus at generators of ker θ). Mathlib does not prove that B_dR is a field, nor construct its filtration or Galois action; A_inf, B_inf of p. 67 are W(𝒪_{k̄̂}^♭) and its p-inversion, available only as 𝕎 (PreTilt R p). This is the ring, not the sheaf 𝔹_dR^+ of §6.

items.name: Lisse ℤ_p-sheaf on X_ét
items.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian adic space or locally noetherian scheme. A lisse ℤ_p-sheaf 𝕃_• on X_ét is an inverse system of sheaves of ℤ/p^n-modules 𝕃_n on X_ét, such that each 𝕃_n is locally on X_ét a constant sheaf associated with a finitely generated ℤ/p^n-module, and such that this inverse system is isomorphic in the procategory to an inverse system for which 𝕃_{n+1}/p^n ≅ 𝕃_n.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/lisse-zp-sheaf (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L0 builds adic coefficients but states 'This construction does not assert the same theory for ℤ_p' (ℓ ≠ p only); no other stage defines lisse ℤ_p-sheaves on adic spaces. Not in Mathlib/Tau Ceti.

items.name: Ẑ_p and lisse Ẑ_p-sheaves on X_proét
items.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian adic space or locally noetherian scheme. Let Ẑ_p = lim_← ℤ/p^n as sheaves on X_proét. A lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf on X_proét is a sheaf 𝕃 of Ẑ_p-modules on X_proét such that locally in X_proét, 𝕃 is isomorphic to Ẑ_p ⊗_{ℤ_p} M, where M is a finitely generated ℤ_p-module.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/lisse-zp-sheaf (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Not in Mathlib/Tau Ceti.

items.name: 𝕃̂_• is a lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf
items.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian adic space over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p), and let 𝕃_• be a lisse ℤ_p-sheaf on X_ét. Then 𝕃 = 𝕃̂_• = lim_← ν^*𝕃_n is a lisse sheaf of Ẑ_p-modules on X_proét. In particular, 𝕃 ⊗_{Ẑ_p} ℚ̂_p is a ℚ̂_p = Ẑ_p[p^{−1}]-local system on X_proét.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/lisse-sheaves-etale-proetale-equivalence (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Proof from Theorem 4.9 and Lemma 3.18.

items.name: Lisse ℤ_p-sheaves on X_ét ≃ lisse Ẑ_p-sheaves on X_proét
items.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian adic space over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p). The functor 𝕃_• ↦ 𝕃̂_• = lim_← ν^*𝕃_n from lisse ℤ_p-sheaves on X_ét to lisse Ẑ_p-sheaves on X_proét is an equivalence of categories.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/lisse-sheaves-etale-proetale-equivalence (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Proof from Theorem 4.9 and Lemma 3.18.

items.name: Vanishing of R^j lim ν^*𝕃_n
items.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian adic space over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p), and 𝕃_• a lisse ℤ_p-sheaf on X_ét. Then R^j lim_← ν^*𝕃_n = 0 for j > 0.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/lisse-sheaves-etale-proetale-equivalence (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. From Lemma 3.18 (repleteness of X_proét).

items.name: Higher direct images of lisse ℤ_p-sheaves for schemes
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be a proper smooth morphism of locally noetherian schemes of characteristic prime to p, and let 𝕃_• be a lisse ℤ_p-sheaf on X_ét. Then the inverse system R^if_ét*𝕃_• of the R^if_ét*𝕃_n is a lisse ℤ_p-sheaf on Y_ét.
items.note: Consequence of proper and smooth base change for schemes. SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2: 'construct sheaf cohomology, localization, proper/smooth base change and compact support'. The paper remarks that even if 𝕃_{n+1}/p^n ≅ 𝕃_n, this may fail for the R^if_ét*𝕃_n.

items.name: R^if_ét*𝕃_• completes to R^if_proét*𝕃̂_•
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be a proper smooth morphism of locally noetherian adic spaces or locally noetherian schemes, and 𝕃_• a lisse ℤ_p-sheaf on X_ét such that R^if_ét*𝕃_• is a lisse ℤ_p-sheaf on Y_ét. As the higher R^j lim_← ν^*𝕃_n vanish, (R^if_ét*𝕃_•)^ = R^if_proét*𝕃̂_•.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/lisse-sheaves-etale-proetale-equivalence (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Uses Proposition 8.2 and Corollary 3.17.

items.name: de Rham lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf
items.statement: Let k be a discretely valued complete nonarchimedean extension of ℚ_p with perfect residue field κ and ring of integers 𝒪_k, and let X be a proper smooth adic space over Spa(k, 𝒪_k). A lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf 𝕃 is said to be de Rham if the associated 𝔹_dR^+-local system 𝕄 = 𝕃 ⊗_{Ẑ_p} 𝔹_dR^+ is associated with some filtered module with integrable connection (ℰ, ∇, Fil^•).
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/de-rham-lisse-sheaf (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. 'Associated' is Definition 7.5 applied to 𝕄 ⊗_{𝔹_dR^+} 𝒪𝔹_dR^+ (Theorem 7.2). Theorem 8.8(ii) uses the notion on a non-proper smooth base Y; the properness in Definition 8.3 is unnecessary (PAPER-SCHOLZE-13/E20).

items.name: B_dR^+-comparison for lisse Ẑ_p-sheaves
items.statement: Let k be a discretely valued complete nonarchimedean extension of ℚ_p with perfect residue field κ, ring of integers 𝒪_k, and algebraic closure k̄, and let X be a proper smooth adic space over Spa(k, 𝒪_k). For any lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf 𝕃 on X_proét with associated 𝔹_dR^+-local system 𝕄 = 𝕃 ⊗_{Ẑ_p} 𝔹_dR^+, there is a Gal(k̄/k)-equivariant isomorphism H^i(X_k̄, 𝕃) ⊗_{ℤ_p} B_dR^+ ≅ H^i(X_k̄, 𝕄).
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/etale-to-bdr-plus-comparison-for-lisse-sheaves (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Proof (pp. 67–68): almost isomorphisms H^i(X_k̄, 𝕃_n) ⊗ A_inf^a ≅ H^i(X_k̄, 𝕃_n ⊗ 𝔸_inf^a) inductively from the primitive comparison Theorem 5.1 (with Proposition 3.15), pass to lim via the almost version of Lemma 3.18, invert p, multiply by ξ^k (Lemma 6.3) to get B_inf/(ker θ)^k-level isomorphisms, and take the limit (Lemma 3.18). Depends on the primitive comparison theorem, which the BMS18 extraction (item 085) found unplanned; CohomologyComparisons:CP.3's 'comparison after B_dR-inversion with p-adic étale cohomology' is for the BMS1 deformation with constant coefficients, not lisse 𝕃.

items.name: H^i(X_k̄, 𝕄) is finite free over B_dR^+
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 8.4, H^i(X_k̄, 𝕄) is a free B_dR^+-module of finite rank, and hence dim_{k̄̂} H^i(X_k̄, gr^0𝕄) = dim_{B_dR}(H^i(X_k̄, 𝕄) ⊗_{B_dR^+} B_dR).
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/etale-to-bdr-plus-comparison-for-lisse-sheaves (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. From Theorem 8.4(a), since H^i(X_k̄, 𝕃) is a finitely generated ℤ_p-module and p is invertible in B_dR^+. CohomologyComparisons:CP.3 plans 'finite freeness in the source scope' only for the constant-coefficient BMS1 deformation.

items.name: Hodge–de Rham degeneration for de Rham coefficients
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 8.4, if 𝕃 is de Rham, with associated filtered module with integrable connection (ℰ, ∇, Fil^•), then the Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence H^{i−j,j}_Hodge(X, ℰ) ⇒ H^i_dR(X, ℰ) degenerates.
items.note: P8: 'apply CohomologyComparisons CP.3–CP.4 to the proper-smooth comparison with connection and tensor compatibility'; for 𝕃 = Ẑ_p (ℰ = 𝒪_X) also CP.3: 'Prove filtration strictness and the Hodge–Tate/de Rham spectral-sequence comparisons in characteristic zero, with proper smoothness'. Proof: freeness of H^i(X_k̄, 𝕄) and Theorem 7.11 give Σ_j dim_k H^{i−j,j}_Hodge(X, ℰ) = dim_k H^i_dR(X, ℰ). For ℰ = 𝒪_X this is the degeneration of Corollary 1.8 (Hodge–de Rham for proper smooth rigid spaces).

items.name: de Rham comparison for de Rham lisse sheaves
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 8.4, if 𝕃 is de Rham with associated (ℰ, ∇, Fil^•), there is a Gal(k̄/k)-equivariant isomorphism H^i(X_k̄, 𝕃) ⊗_{ℤ_p} B_dR ≅ H^i_dR(X, ℰ) ⊗_k B_dR preserving filtrations.
items.note: P8: 'the proper-smooth comparison with connection and tensor compatibility'; CP.3 for constant coefficients ('the comparison after B_dR-inversion with p-adic étale cohomology' and 'When X descends to a proper smooth X_0/K, compare that deformation with H_dR(X_0/K) tensor_K B_dR^+'). Follows from 8.4(a) and Theorem 7.11. Theorem 8.4 is the introduction's Theorem 1.6; for 𝕃 = Ẑ_p this gives the de Rham comparison behind Corollary 1.8.

items.name: Hodge–Tate decomposition for de Rham lisse sheaves
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 8.4, if 𝕃 is de Rham with associated (ℰ, ∇, Fil^•), there is a Gal(k̄/k)-equivariant isomorphism H^i(X_k̄, 𝕃) ⊗_{ℤ_p} k̄̂ ≅ ⨁_j H^{i−j,j}_Hodge(X, ℰ) ⊗_k k̄̂(−j). For 𝕃 = Ẑ_p this reads H^i(X_k̄, ℤ_p) ⊗ k̄̂ ≅ ⨁_j H^{i−j}(X, Ω_X^j) ⊗_k k̄̂(−j).
items.note: P8 ('the proper-smooth comparison with connection'); CP.3 'Hodge–Tate/de Rham spectral-sequence comparisons' for constant coefficients. Follows directly from Theorem 7.11(b) and 8.4(a); trivial-coefficient case via Remark 7.12.

items.name: Relative Poincaré lemma
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be a smooth morphism of smooth adic spaces over Spa(k, 𝒪_k), of relative dimension d. By composition with the projection Ω_X^1 → Ω_{X/Y}^1, we get the relative derivation ∇_{X/Y} : 𝒪𝔹_{dR,X}^+ → 𝒪𝔹_{dR,X}^+ ⊗_{𝒪_X} Ω_{X/Y}^1, and the following sequence is exact: 0 → 𝔹_{dR,X}^+ ⊗_{f_proét^*𝔹_{dR,Y}^+} f_proét^*𝒪𝔹_{dR,Y}^+ → 𝒪𝔹_{dR,X}^+ →^{∇_{X/Y}} 𝒪𝔹_{dR,X}^+ ⊗_{𝒪_X} Ω_{X/Y}^1 →^{∇_{X/Y}} ⋯ →^{∇_{X/Y}} 𝒪𝔹_{dR,X}^+ ⊗_{𝒪_X} Ω_{X/Y}^d → 0.
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational: 'Prove rational local acyclicity, filtration strictness and the relative Poincaré lemma'. Proof: reduce to X = 𝕋^n → Y = 𝕋^{n−d} and use Proposition 6.10 (strengthened form per the corrigendum, with the corrected 𝒪𝔹_dR^+).

items.name: Strict exactness of the relative Poincaré sequence
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 8.5, the exact sequence 0 → 𝔹_{dR,X}^+ ⊗_{f_proét^*𝔹_{dR,Y}^+} f_proét^*𝒪𝔹_{dR,Y}^+ → 𝒪𝔹_{dR,X}^+ → 𝒪𝔹_{dR,X}^+ ⊗ Ω_{X/Y}^1 → ⋯ → 𝒪𝔹_{dR,X}^+ ⊗ Ω_{X/Y}^d → 0 is strict exact with respect to the filtration giving Ω_{X/Y}^i degree i.
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational: 'filtration strictness and the relative Poincaré lemma'.

items.name: Relative base change for gr^0𝒪𝔹_dR
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be a proper smooth morphism of smooth adic spaces over Spa(k, 𝒪_k). Let 𝒜 be a locally free 𝒪_X-module of finite rank. Then the morphism (Rf_proét*𝒜) ⊗_{𝒪_Y} gr^0𝒪𝔹_{dR,Y} → Rf_proét*(𝒜 ⊗_{𝒪_X} gr^0𝒪𝔹_{dR,X}) is an isomorphism in the derived category.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-pushforward-of-graded-structural-sheaf (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Relative analogue of Lemma 7.13. Proof via Lemma 5.2 charts Y → 𝕋^m, Ỹ = Y ×_{𝕋^m} 𝕋̃_K^m, a simplicial cover X_• with charts X_i → 𝕋^n over Y → 𝕋^m, and Lemma 8.7; then Proposition 6.16(i), Corollary 3.17(ii), Proposition 9.2(ii).

items.name: Lemma 8.7(i): completed structure sheaf on W_i, W̃_i
items.statement: In the proof of Lemma 8.6 (Y affinoid with an étale map Y → 𝕋^m that is a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps, K the completed algebraic closure of k, Ỹ = Y ×_{𝕋^m} 𝕋̃_K^m, U pro-finite étale over Ỹ, X_• an open simplicial cover of X with étale maps X_i → 𝕋^n over the projection 𝕋^n → 𝕋^m, X̃_i = X_i ×_{𝕋^n} 𝕋̃_K^n), with all completed tensor products being completed tensor products of Banach spaces: Let W_i = U ×_Y X_i and W̃_i = U ×_Ỹ X̃_i. Then W̃_i is pro-finite étale over X̃_i, 𝒪̂_X(W_i) = 𝒪̂_Y(U) ⊗̂_{𝒪_Y(Y)} 𝒪_X(X_i), and 𝒪̂_X(W̃_i) = 𝒪̂_X(W_i) ⊗̂_{K⟨T_{m+1}^{±1},…,T_n^{±1}⟩} K⟨T_{m+1}^{±1/p^∞},…,T_n^{±1/p^∞}⟩.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-completed-structure-sheaf-computations (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Proof uses Lemma 6.18, [17, Theorem 7.9, Proposition 6.18] (almost purity / fibre products of perfectoids) and ℤ_p^{n−m}-invariants as in Lemma 5.5.

items.name: Lemma 8.7(ii): flatness up to bounded p-power
items.statement: In the proof of Lemma 8.6 (Y affinoid with an étale map Y → 𝕋^m that is a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps, K the completed algebraic closure of k, Ỹ = Y ×_{𝕋^m} 𝕋̃_K^m, U pro-finite étale over Ỹ, X_• an open simplicial cover of X with étale maps X_i → 𝕋^n over the projection 𝕋^n → 𝕋^m, X̃_i = X_i ×_{𝕋^n} 𝕋̃_K^n), with all completed tensor products being completed tensor products of Banach spaces: The ring 𝒪̂_Y^+(U) is flat over 𝒪_Y^+(Y) up to a bounded p-power: that is, there is some integer N such that for all 𝒪_Y^+(Y)-modules M, the group Tor_1^{𝒪_Y^+(Y)}(M, 𝒪̂_Y^+(U)) is annihilated by p^N.
items.note: Planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-completed-structure-sheaf-computations (PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, merged before this extraction. Proof: almost flat over 𝒪̂_Y^+(Ỹ) by almost purity; 𝒪̂_Y^+(Ỹ) is up to bounded p-power 𝒪_Y^+(Y) ⊗̂_{𝒪_k⟨T^{±1}⟩} 𝒪_K⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩ (Lemma 6.18), topologically free over 𝒪_Y^+(Y) ⊗̂_{𝒪_k} 𝒪_K.

items.name: Lemma 8.7(iii): Čech differentials have closed image
items.statement: In the proof of Lemma 8.6 (Y affinoid with an étale map Y → 𝕋^m that is a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps, K the completed algebraic closure of k, Ỹ = Y ×_{𝕋^m} 𝕋̃_K^m, U pro-finite étale over Ỹ, X_• an open simplicial cover of X with étale maps X_i → 𝕋^n over the projection 𝕋^n → 𝕋^m, X̃_i = X_i ×_{𝕋^n} 𝕋̃_K^n), with all completed tensor products being completed tensor products of Banach spaces: In the complex C : 0 → 𝒜(X_1) → 𝒜(X_2) → ⋯ associated with the simplicial covering X_• of X, computing (Rf_proét*𝒜)(Y), all boundary maps have closed image.
items.note: Follows from Kiehl's finiteness theorem [12]. AdicSpacesPartII:R3: 'Establish Kiehl-type proper finiteness/coherence'.

items.name: Lemma 8.7(iv): gr^0𝒪𝔹_dR on W_i
items.statement: In the proof of Lemma 8.6 (Y affinoid with an étale map Y → 𝕋^m that is a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps, K the completed algebraic closure of k, Ỹ = Y ×_{𝕋^m} 𝕋̃_K^m, U pro-finite étale over Ỹ, X_• an open simplicial cover of X with étale maps X_i → 𝕋^n over the projection 𝕋^n → 𝕋^m, X̃_i = X_i ×_{𝕋^n} 𝕋̃_K^n), with all completed tensor products being completed tensor products of Banach spaces: (gr^0𝒪𝔹_{dR,X})(W_i) = 𝒪̂_X(W_i)[V_1,…,V_m], where V_a is the image of t^{−1}log([T_a^♭]/T_a) in gr^0𝒪𝔹_{dR,X}. Moreover, H^q(W_i, gr^0𝒪𝔹_{dR,X}) = 0 for q > 0.
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational: 'Prove rational local acyclicity'. Proof: Čech cohomology of W̃_i → W_i as in Proposition 6.16(i), starting from part (i).

items.name: Relative B_dR^+-comparison
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be a proper smooth morphism of smooth adic spaces over Spa(k, 𝒪_k). Let 𝕃 be a lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf on X_proét, and let 𝕄 = 𝕃 ⊗_{Ẑ_p} 𝔹_{dR,X}^+ be the associated 𝔹_{dR,X}^+-local system. Assume that R^if_proét*𝕃 is a lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf on Y_proét. Then there is a canonical isomorphism R^if_proét*𝕄 ≅ R^if_proét*𝕃 ⊗_{Ẑ_p} 𝔹_{dR,Y}^+. In particular, R^if_proét*𝕄 is a 𝔹_{dR,Y}^+-local system on Y, which is associated with R^if_proét*𝕃.
items.note: P8 ('Shared relative period sheaves'): 'apply CohomologyComparisons CP.3–CP.4 to the proper-smooth comparison with connection and tensor compatibility'; the Gauss–Manin connection makes this the relative comparison. Only abelian degree-one families are planned more specifically (HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T1). Proof: on Y_proét/Y_K, start from Corollary 5.12 ((R^if_ét*𝕃') ⊗ 𝒪_Y^{+a}/p ≅ R^if_ét*(𝕃' ⊗ 𝒪_X^{+a}/p)), tilt to 𝒪^{+a♭}/π^m, pass to 𝔸_inf^a/[π]^m and to limits with Lemma 3.18, then as in Theorem 8.4.

items.name: Relative Hodge cohomology is locally free
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be a proper smooth morphism of smooth adic spaces over Spa(k, 𝒪_k). Let 𝕃 be a lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf on X_proét, and let 𝕄 = 𝕃 ⊗_{Ẑ_p} 𝔹_{dR,X}^+ be the associated 𝔹_{dR,X}^+-local system. Assume that R^if_proét*𝕃 is a lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf on Y_proét. Assume that 𝕃 is de Rham, and let (ℰ, ∇, Fil^•) be the associated filtered 𝒪_X-module with integrable connection. Then the relative Hodge cohomology R^{i−j,j}f_Hodge*(ℰ) (= R^if_*(gr^j DR(ℰ)) for the relative de Rham complex DR(ℰ) = (0 → ℰ → ℰ ⊗ Ω_{X/Y}^1 → ⋯)) is a locally free 𝒪_Y-module of finite rank for all i, j.
items.note: P8 ('Shared relative period sheaves'): 'apply CohomologyComparisons CP.3–CP.4 to the proper-smooth comparison with connection and tensor compatibility'; the Gauss–Manin connection makes this the relative comparison. Only abelian degree-one families are planned more specifically (HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T1). Proof: filtered quasi-isomorphism Rf_proét*(DR(ℰ)) ⊗_{𝒪_Y} 𝒪𝔹_{dR,Y} ≅ (Rf_proét*𝕄) ⊗_{𝔹_{dR,Y}^+} 𝒪𝔹_{dR,Y} (Lemma 8.6, Proposition 8.5); on gr^0 the right side is locally free over gr^0𝒪𝔹_{dR,Y}, which is locally faithfully flat over 𝒪_Y.

items.name: Relative Hodge–de Rham degeneration
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be a proper smooth morphism of smooth adic spaces over Spa(k, 𝒪_k). Let 𝕃 be a lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf on X_proét, and let 𝕄 = 𝕃 ⊗_{Ẑ_p} 𝔹_{dR,X}^+ be the associated 𝔹_{dR,X}^+-local system. Assume that R^if_proét*𝕃 is a lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf on Y_proét. Assume that 𝕃 is de Rham with associated (ℰ, ∇, Fil^•). Then the relative Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence R^{i−j,j}f_Hodge*(ℰ) ⇒ R^if_dR*(ℰ) degenerates.
items.note: P8 ('Shared relative period sheaves'): 'apply CohomologyComparisons CP.3–CP.4 to the proper-smooth comparison with connection and tensor compatibility'; the Gauss–Manin connection makes this the relative comparison. Only abelian degree-one families are planned more specifically (HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T1). Proof: R^if_dR*(ℰ) ⊗_{𝒪_Y} 𝒪𝔹_{dR,Y} ≅ (R^if_proét*𝕄) ⊗_{𝔹_{dR,Y}^+} 𝒪𝔹_{dR,Y} compatibly with filtration and connection; count ranks of locally free modules.

items.name: Higher direct images of de Rham sheaves are de Rham
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be a proper smooth morphism of smooth adic spaces over Spa(k, 𝒪_k). Let 𝕃 be a lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf on X_proét, and let 𝕄 = 𝕃 ⊗_{Ẑ_p} 𝔹_{dR,X}^+ be the associated 𝔹_{dR,X}^+-local system. Assume that R^if_proét*𝕃 is a lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf on Y_proét. Assume that 𝕃 is de Rham with associated (ℰ, ∇, Fil^•). Then R^if_proét*𝕃 is de Rham, with associated filtered 𝒪_Y-module with integrable connection given by R^if_dR*(ℰ) (with its Hodge filtration and Gauss–Manin connection).
items.note: P8 ('Shared relative period sheaves'): 'apply CohomologyComparisons CP.3–CP.4 to the proper-smooth comparison with connection and tensor compatibility'; the Gauss–Manin connection makes this the relative comparison. Only abelian degree-one families are planned more specifically (HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T1). Here 'de Rham' is Definition 8.3 applied on the (not necessarily proper) smooth space Y; see PAPER-SCHOLZE-13/E20.

items.name: Hypothesis of Theorem 8.8 holds for algebraic families
items.statement: In Theorem 8.8, the assumption that R^if_proét*𝕃 is a lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf on Y_proét is satisfied whenever f : X → Y and 𝕃 come as the analytifications of corresponding algebraic objects.
items.note: By Theorem 9.3 and smooth proper base change for schemes (remark after Theorem 9.3), plus Proposition 8.2. Depends on ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H5 (Theorem 9.3) and SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2, but no stage states this consequence.

items.name: Relative GAGA over an affinoid base: coherent sheaves
items.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field, let A be a complete topologically finitely generated Tate algebra over K, and let S_0 = Spec A, with corresponding adic space S = Spa(A, A°). Further, let f_0 : X_0 → S_0 be a proper morphism of schemes, and let f : X → S be the corresponding morphism of adic spaces. Then the category of coherent 𝒪_{X_0}-modules is equivalent to that of coherent 𝒪_X-modules.
items.note: Planned: AdicSpacesPartII:R3/proper-gaga-coherent-equivalence (AdicSpacesPartII packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/AdicSpacesPartII.json, merged before this extraction. Main result of Köpf's thesis [13]. AdicSpacesPartII:R1 plans only the absolute case: 'Construct the adic analytification of a finite-type scheme over the base field … Establish the properness comparison and the proper GAGA results required for algebraic coefficient sheaves'; AdicEtaleGeometry:A2 supplies 'the relative constructions over an affinoid pair' (analytification) but not relative GAGA. data/library-coverage.json: no analytification or GAGA in either library.

items.name: Relative GAGA over an affinoid base: higher direct images
items.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field, let A be a complete topologically finitely generated Tate algebra over K, and let S_0 = Spec A, with corresponding adic space S = Spa(A, A°). Further, let f_0 : X_0 → S_0 be a proper morphism of schemes, and let f : X → S be the corresponding morphism of adic spaces. Let ℱ_0 be a coherent 𝒪_{X_0}-module with analytification ℱ on X. Then for all i ≥ 0, R^if_*ℱ is coherent and equal to the analytification of R^if_{0*}ℱ_0.
items.note: Planned: AdicSpacesPartII:R3/proper-gaga (AdicSpacesPartII packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/AdicSpacesPartII.json, merged before this extraction. Köpf [13].

items.name: Coherent sheaves on the étale site of an affinoid are acyclic
items.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field; all adic spaces are locally of finite type over Spa(K, 𝒪_K). Let ℱ be a coherent module on an affinoid adic space X. Then the association mapping any affinoid étale U → X to 𝒪_U(U) ⊗_{𝒪_X(X)} ℱ(X) is a sheaf ℱ_ét on X_ét. For i > 0, the higher cohomology group H^i(X_ét, ℱ_ét) = 0 vanishes.
items.note: From [11, Proposition 3.2.5] (de Jong–van der Put). AdicSpacesPartII:R3 plans 'the affinoid coherent-sheaf equivalence, acyclicity' in the analytic topology only; no stage plans étale acyclicity of coherent sheaves.

items.name: Étale base change for coherent cohomology of proper maps
items.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field; all adic spaces are locally of finite type over Spa(K, 𝒪_K). Let g : T → S be an étale morphism of affinoid adic spaces. Let f : X → S be proper. Let ℱ_X be a coherent 𝒪_X-module, let Y = X ×_S T, and let ℱ_Y be the pullback of ℱ_X to Y. Then for all i, we have an isomorphism H^i(X, ℱ_X) ⊗_{𝒪_S(S)} 𝒪_T(T) ≅ H^i(Y, ℱ_Y). In particular, (R^if_*ℱ)_ét = R^if_ét*ℱ_ét.
items.note: Planned: AdicSpacesPartII:R3/proper-coherent-base-change (AdicSpacesPartII packet) states it, in research/blueprint/packets/AdicSpacesPartII.json, merged before this extraction. Proof: by [11, Proposition 3.2.2] reduce to T ⊂ S rational (Kiehl [12], Satz 3.5) and T → S finite étale (Čech complex and flatness of 𝒪_T(T) over 𝒪_S(S)).

items.name: Algebraic vs analytic étale direct images (Huber)
items.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field, let f_0 : X_0 → S_0 be a proper morphism of schemes over K, let S be an adic space locally of finite type over Spa(K, 𝒪_K), and let S → S_0 be a morphism of locally ringed topological spaces, which induces via base-change a proper morphism of adic spaces f : X → S. Let m be an integer which is invertible in K. Let 𝕃_0 be a ℤ/mℤ-sheaf on X_{0ét} which is locally on X_{0ét} the constant sheaf associated with a finitely generated ℤ/mℤ-module. Let 𝕃 be the associated sheaf on X_ét. Then R^if_ét*𝕃 is the analytification of R^if_{0ét*}𝕃_0.
items.note: Cited from [9, Theorem 3.7.2] (Huber). ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H5: 'Prove the cases of Hub96 Theorems 3.7.2 and 3.8.1 … proper algebraic/analytic direct-image comparison'. Note H5 is scoped to 'the cases … used in ECD §27'.

items.name: Local constancy of R^if_*𝕃 for smooth proper or point base
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 9.3, if X_0 → S_0 is smooth or S_0 is a point, then R^if_{0ét*}𝕃_0 is locally on S_{0ét} the constant sheaf associated with a finitely generated ℤ/mℤ-module; thus the same is true for R^if_ét*𝕃.
items.note: Smooth and proper base change and finiteness for schemes. SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2: 'construct sheaf cohomology, localization, proper/smooth base change and compact support'; the analytic half then follows from Theorem 9.3.

items.name: R° is topologically finitely generated for reduced affinoid R
items.statement: Let K be an algebraically closed nonarchimedean field, and let R be a topologically finitely generated Tate K-algebra, i.e. a quotient of K⟨T_1,…,T_n⟩ for some n. Assume that R is reduced. Then R° is a topologically finitely generated 𝒪_K-algebra: that is, there is a surjection 𝒪_K⟨T_1,…,T_n⟩ → R° for some n.
items.note: From [3, Section 6.4.1, Corollary 5] (BGR; Grauert–Remmert finiteness). Tau Ceti has Huber rings, restricted power series and Spa (TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber, TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace) but grep for 6.4.1 / reduced affinoid / R° finiteness finds nothing; no atlas stage cites it.

items.name: S° is finite over R° for finite reduced S
items.statement: Let K be an algebraically closed nonarchimedean field and R a reduced topologically finitely generated Tate K-algebra. If S is a finite reduced R-algebra, then S° is a finite R°-algebra.
items.note: From [3, Section 6.4.1, Corollary 5]. Not planned; not in Mathlib/Tau Ceti.

prerequisites.citation: G. Faltings, Almost étale extensions, Astérisque 279 (2002), 185–270
prerequisites.why: Faltings's almost purity and comparison method: §2 formalizes his almost finiteness (§3 Theorem 8), and Theorem 1.3 and Remark 1.4 are closely related to his results.

prerequisites.citation: O. Gabber, L. Ramero, Almost Ring Theory, Lecture Notes in Math. 1800 (2003)
prerequisites.why: Almost-module theory used in §2 (Proposition 2.7 is their Lemma 2.3.18) and almost faithfully flat descent (Lemma 4.12).

prerequisites.citation: R. Huber, Étale cohomology of rigid analytic varieties and adic spaces, Aspects of Mathematics E30 (1996)
prerequisites.why: The étale site of adic spaces, local structure of smooth maps (1.6.10), openness of étale maps, proper base change and the comparison Theorem 3.7.2 used in §§3, 5, 9.

prerequisites.citation: R. Kiehl, Der Endlichkeitssatz für eigentliche Abbildungen in der nichtarchimedischen Funktionentheorie, Invent. Math. 2 (1967), 191–214
prerequisites.why: Finiteness of coherent cohomology of proper rigid spaces; the model for the Cartan–Serre argument of §5 and used in §§8–9.

prerequisites.citation: O. Brinon, Représentations p-adiques cristallines et de de Rham dans le cas relatif, Mém. Soc. Math. France 112 (2008)
prerequisites.why: Relative period rings, the Galois cohomology of gr⁰𝒪B_dR (Proposition 6.16) and the recipe for the corrected 𝒪B⁺_dR.

prerequisites.citation: F. Andreatta, A. Iovita, Comparison isomorphisms for smooth formal schemes, J. Inst. Math. Jussieu 12 (2013), 77–151
prerequisites.why: The model for the proof of the de Rham comparison (Theorem 1.6/8.4) and the notation 𝔹^∇+_dR.

prerequisites.citation: P. Colmez, Espaces de Banach de dimension finie, J. Inst. Math. Jussieu 1 (2002), 331–439
prerequisites.why: Sympathetic algebras, used for Proposition 4.8 (affinoid perfectoids form a basis in general).

prerequisites.citation: J. Tate, p-divisible groups, Proc. Conf. Local Fields (Driebergen 1966), Springer (1967), 158–183
prerequisites.why: Galois cohomology of ℂ_p(i) used in §6, and the question on the Hodge–Tate decomposition answered by Corollary 1.8.

prerequisites.citation: U. Köpf, Über eigentliche Familien algebraischer Varietäten über affinoiden Räumen, Schriftenreihe Math. Inst. Univ. Münster, 2. Serie, Heft 7 (1974)
prerequisites.why: Relative GAGA over an affinoid base (Theorem 9.1).

routes.reason: P8 ('Shared relative period sheaves') and its early cut P8:local-rational were written from this paper, and the PadicHodgeTheory P7 packet (research/blueprint/packets/PadicHodgeTheory--P7.json, scope P7, P8, R06.1–R06.4) already has nodes for §§6–8 statement by statement: the period sheaves and their values on affinoid perfectoids, the corrected 𝒪𝔹⁺_dR and its local structure, Faltings's extension, the pushforwards ν_*, the functor of Theorem 7.6 with Lemmas 7.7–7.10, the comparisons of Theorems 7.11, 8.4 and 8.8, and Theorem 4.9. Those items are now planned, and this route names them as planned items for which the paper is the source. What remains missing is the primitive comparison and finiteness theorem with its proof (Theorems 1.1, 1.3 and 5.1, Lemmas 5.3–5.9, Corollary 5.12, Lemma 4.12), and a few remarks (1.9, 7.12, 8.9, the Rapoport–Zink claim). Accepted extractions route the primitive comparison and finiteness to P8 (PAPER-ZAVYALOV-25 route 7 and PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-18 route 14, both accepted on review; PAPER-HEUER-25 route 1 is awaiting review). The P7 packet itself records it as having no owner and requests it from CohomologyComparisons CP.3, pending a restructure decision; P8's blueprint should settle that request in line with these accepted routes. The integral inputs the packet requests from AInfCohomology AI.3 (Lemmas 3.18, 5.5 and 5.11, and the integral cases of Theorem 6.5 and Corollary 6.6) are moved to route 5.

§2's theory of almost finitely generated 𝒪-modules extends P0's almost mathematics. The PerfectoidSpaces packet (research/blueprint/packets/PerfectoidSpaces--P0.json) already plans almost finite generation and presentation over a basic setup, its dependence only on M^a, and the lifting of almost finite generation along an adically complete base (P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented, P0/adic-almost-projective-modules); the rank-one theory of Sch13 (≈_ε, Theorem 2.5, the elementary divisors γ_M and λ of Propositions 2.10–2.11, Proposition 2.7, Lemma 2.12) is not there and belongs in P0. The §4 statements that P6's node PerfectoidSpaces:P6/scholze-2013-affinoid-perfectoid-comparison states (Definition 4.3(i), Example 4.4, Lemmas 4.5(i) and 4.6) are planned, and this route names them. The integral §4 statements the extraction sent to P2 and P6 are moved to route 5 (AInfCohomology AI.3).

A1 plans 'the pro-étale extension' of the étale site with Scholze's corrected covering definition, and the AdicEtaleGeometry packet (research/blueprint/packets/AdicEtaleGeometry.json, review accepted) has a node for each §3 statement, citing it: pro-X_ét and |U|, G-fsets and G-pfsets with corrected covers, Proposition 3.5, Lemma 3.6, the corrected Proposition 3.7, Lemmas 3.10–3.11, Propositions 3.12, 3.13 (without the removed sentence) and 3.15, and ν. ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H0 has Proposition 3.7(iii), Lemma 3.16 and Corollary 3.17. All of the route's items are now planned; the route stands as a source route naming planned items. Lemma 3.18, which the PadicHodgeTheory packet requests from AInfCohomology AI.3, is moved to route 5.

§9's miscellany covers relative GAGA over an affinoid base (Köpf, Theorem 9.1) and the étale acyclicity and base change of coherent sheaves (Proposition 9.2). It also covers topological finite generation of R° for a reduced affinoid R (Theorem 9.4). These extend R1's analytification over a base field and R3's coherent-sheaf theory. The AdicSpacesPartII packet (research/blueprint/packets/AdicSpacesPartII.json, review accepted) already plans Theorem 9.1 (R3/proper-gaga-coherent-equivalence, R3/proper-gaga) and Proposition 9.2(ii) (R3/proper-coherent-base-change); those items are now planned. Proposition 9.2(i) and Theorem 9.4 remain missing, as the route proposes.

AI.3 constructs 'the completed integral structure sheaf, its tilt and the Witt A_inf,X sheaf' on the pro-étale site with the corrigendum's corrected covers, and 'a toric perfectoid cover ... its continuous group cochains'; PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational imports the integral A_inf sheaf from it. Its stage text is written for generic fibres of smooth formal schemes, but PadicHodgeTheory's P7 packet requests from AI.3 exactly these statements of this paper for every locally noetherian adic space over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p): O_X⁺/pⁿ ≅ Ô_X⁺/pⁿ with Ô_X⁺(U) flat and p-adically complete (Lemma 4.2(iii)); affinoid perfectoid objects with Û independent of the presentation and the basis (Corollary 4.7, Proposition 4.8); Lemma 4.10; the tilted sheaf and Lemma 5.11 (arXiv v2 Lemma 5.10); the integral cases of Theorem 6.5 and Corollary 6.6; Lemma 3.18; and the toric Koszul computation of Lemma 5.5. Sch13 is the source that extends AI.3 to that generality. The extraction had sent these to PerfectoidSpaces P2 and P6 (and Lemmas 3.18 and 5.5 to AdicEtaleGeometry A1 and PadicHodgeTheory P8), which would make a second owner of the completed integral structure sheaf; PerfectoidSpaces:P6/scholze-2013-affinoid-perfectoid-comparison keeps what it states (Definition 4.3(i), Example 4.4, Lemmas 4.5(i) and 4.6).
